definition_zh: 起源；发源；创始；引起；起始于
definition_en: to begin to exist, to come from a particular place or cause, or to create something new
core_image: 山间一眼细小的泉水，后来汇成整条大河
scene: 关于这条河的记录很少，只知它从高山深处流出。The river originates in the mountains far to the north.
sceneCN: 这里 originate 是「发源于」（第 1 个义项：从某处开始存在）；句意为这条河发源于遥远的北方群山之中。

pos.zh: 动词：起源；发源；创始；引起

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「起源；出身；原点」
由本词根加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「最初的；原创的」
由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「起源；创始；发起」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀 -or 构成，义为「创始人；发明者」

senses.title: To begin in a place
senses.definition: to start to exist in a particular place or at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地点或某个时间开始存在
senses.example: The custom originates in the farming villages of the south.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗起源于南方的农耕村落。
senses.why: Latin origo is the rising of a river at its source, and oriri is to rise, so to originate is to well up from a first point.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 origo 本指河流从源头涌出，oriri 意为「升起」，所以 originate 就是从一个起始点涌出来。

senses.title: To come from a cause
senses.definition: to have its cause in something particular, such as a person, thing, or event
senses.definitionCN: 其成因在于某一特定的人、事或事件
senses.example: The noise originates from a pipe under the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音来自厨房地板下面的一根管道。
senses.why: A source can be a place or a cause: once the noun means where something came from, it covers both the spring and the reason.
senses.whyCN: 源头既可以是地点，也可以是原因：一旦名词表示「事物来处」，它就同时涵盖泉水与缘由。

senses.title: To be created or invented
senses.definition: to create something new, such as a system, style, or method
senses.definitionCN: 创造新的事物，如制度、风格或方法
senses.example: The company originated in a small workshop in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司最初由北方一间小工坊起家。
senses.why: The intransitive verb gained a transitive partner: if a river originates, a person can originate a river of their own.
senses.whyCN: 这个不及物动词后来有了及物用法：河流可以发源，人也可以让一条河从他这里发源。

senses.title: To start something anew
senses.definition: to start an activity, process, or event, often as its very first step
senses.definitionCN: 开始某项活动、过程或事件，常指其最初的一步
senses.example: The procedure originated with a request sent by post.
senses.exampleCN: 这一程序始于一份邮寄来的申请。
senses.why: Starting is the moment of birth, so originate can describe the first motion of anything that then runs on.
senses.whyCN: 开始就是诞生的那一刻，所以 originate 也能描述任何随后延续的事物迈出的第一步。

senses.title: Originating in: the technical source
senses.definition: in medicine and computing, to start in a specific organ, server, or location
senses.definitionCN: 在医学与计算机语境中，指从某个器官、服务器或位置开始
senses.example: The urgent message originated at a server in another country.
senses.exampleCN: 这条紧急讯息是从另一个国家的服务器发出的。
senses.why: Technical use keeps the plain source idea but needs a precise point of departure for signals and symptoms.
senses.whyCN: 技术语境保留了朴素的「来处」含义，只是为信号与症状指定了精确的出发点。

intro.en: Originate comes from Latin origo, a rising or a source, which is built on oriri, to rise.
intro.cn: originate 来自拉丁语 origo（升起、源头），后者建立在 oriri（升起）之上。

items.en: Oriri means to rise, to come into view, and is used of the sun and of rivers.
items.cn: oriri 意为升起、出现，用于太阳，也用于河流。

items.en: Origo means a rising, a beginning, or a source, including birth and noble descent.
items.cn: origo 意为升起、开端或源头，也包括出身与高贵血统。

items.en: The later Latin verb originare develops the sense of taking ones rise from something.
items.cn: 较晚的拉丁语动词 originare 发展出「从某物获得开始」的含义。

items.en: French originer passes the verb form into English channels.
items.cn: 法语 originer 把这套动词形式带入英语通道。

items.en: English originate is first recorded in the seventeenth century; the exact source form is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 originate 首见于十七世纪；其确切的借入形式来源不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same source family; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for starting and coming from.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「源头」词族；近义组收其他表示开始与来自的动词。

entries.definition: the point or place where something begins
entries.definitionCN: 事物起始的点或地方；起源。

entries.definition: existing from the first and not copied
the act of bringing something into being
to happen or appear, usually of problems or situations
entries.definitionCN: 发生；出现，多用于问题或情况。

entries.definition: to be caused by or come from a particular source
to come or obtain something from a source, often in linguistics
entries.definitionCN: 来自；获得，多用于语言学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real river-source root and the phrases that originate actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「河源」词根，以及 originate 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Origo is a rising river: originate is the moment water first clears the stones.
normal.cn: origo 是河水的涌出：originate 就是水第一次漫过石头的那一刻。

normal.en: Origin, original and originate all share the root oriri, to rise.
normal.cn: origin、original 与 originate 共有词根 oriri，意为「升起」。

normal.en: The phrase originate from asks where it came from; originate in asks where it began.
normal.cn: originate from 问它从哪里来；originate in 问它在哪开始。

normal.en: The idea is credited with a person by originate with.
normal.cn: originate with 用来把某个想法归功于某个人。

normal.en: Science uses originated in a tissue to name the exact point where a symptom starts.
normal.cn: 科学语境用 originated in a tissue 来标明症状开始的精确位置。

abstract.en: Picture a needle-thin spring high in the rocks; the great river below is the same water.
abstract.cn: 想象高处岩缝里一眼细如针的泉水，下方的滔滔大河就是同一股水。

abstract.en: Trace a rumour backwards until one person first said it: that person is where it originated.
abstract.cn: 顺着流言往回追，直到第一个开口的人：那个人就是它起源的地方。

abstract.en: A spark leaves the flint and becomes the fire; a spark is how a cause originates.
abstract.cn: 火星从燧石上飞出，最后成为火焰；一个火星就是起因怎样发源的样子。

examples.en: Many English words originate from Latin verbs.
examples.cn: 许多英语单词源自拉丁语动词。

examples.en: The fire appears to have originated in the storage room.
examples.cn: 火灾似乎是从储藏室开始的。

examples.en: Nobody knows who originated the custom of eating dumplings at the festival.
examples.cn: 没人知道是谁首创了在节日吃饺子的习俗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，瑞珍」——瑞珍站在泉眼边说，一切从这里开始；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 oriri（升起；涌出）→ origo（涌出；起源；出身）→ originare → 英语 originated / originate，核心义「从某一点涌出、开始」。

sensesIntro.en: Originate begins with a river springing from a source, then the cause of a noise, then a person creating something, and finally the precise technical point where a thing starts.
sensesIntro.cn: originate 先是河水从源头涌出，再指噪音的成因，接着指人创造新事物，最后指技术语境中事物开始的精确位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin spring at the foot of a cliff, and the wide river it becomes.
core.cn: 核心意象：峭壁脚下一线细泉，以及它后来变成的宽阔大河。

branches.en: The place branch: a custom or a river begins at one point in space.
branches.cn: 地点分支：习俗或河流在空间中的某一点开始。

branches.en: The cause branch: the source is also the reason a thing happens.
branches.cn: 原因分支：源头同时也是事物发生的原因。

branches.en: The creation branch: a person can be the source of something new.
branches.cn: 创造分支：人也可以成为新事物的源头。

branches.en: The start branch: to originate is to take the first step.
branches.cn: 开端分支：originate 就是迈出第一步。

branches.en: The technical branch: signals and symptoms have exact points of origin.
branches.cn: 技术分支：信号与症状都有精确的起始点。

intro.en: Originate is built on the Latin noun for a source, and English adds -ate, -ion, -or and -al to build the family.
intro.cn: originate 建立在表示「源头」的拉丁名词之上，英语再用 -ate、-ion、-or、-al 扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin oriri, origo and originare are recorded, so the root is certain; the exact route into English is less clear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oriri、origo 与 originare 均有文献记录，词根是确定的；进入英语的确切路径则不那么清楚。

definition_zh: 起源；创始；发起；起源过程
definition_en: the act of bringing something into existence, or the state of beginning at a particular point
core_image: 一只手从泉眼里捧起第一捧水，把它装进杯子
scene: 会议上争论激烈，大家想知道这项计划是谁最先提出的。Nobody could agree about the origination of the proposal.
sceneCN: 这里 origination 是「起源、最初产生」（第 1 个义项：事物开始存在的过程）；句意为没有人能就这项提案的起源达成一致。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「起源；创始」，本词由它加名词后缀构成
由动词加表示施动者的后缀 -or 构成，义为「创始人；发起者」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「有创造力的；原创的」
同根形容词，义为「最初的；原创的」

senses.title: The act of beginning
senses.definition: the process by which something first comes into existence or starts
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最初出现或开始的过程
senses.example: Scholars still debate the origination of the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们仍在争论这首诗的起源。
senses.why: The suffix -ion turns the verb into the name of the whole action, so origination is the springing up itself, not the spring.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成整个动作的名称，所以 origination 是「涌出」这个动作本身，而不是那眼泉。

senses.title: The act of creating
senses.definition: the act of creating or establishing something new, such as a company or a method
senses.definitionCN: 建立或创立新事物的行为，如公司或方法
senses.example: The origination of the bank dates from a single loan in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行的创始可以追溯到山区的一笔贷款。
senses.why: With a person as the subject, the action moves from simply happening to deliberately making something happen.
senses.whyCN: 当主语是人时，这个动作就从「自然发生」变成「有意促成」。

senses.title: The point of origin
senses.definition: the place or moment from which something is said to come
senses.definitionCN: 被认定的事物来处或起始时刻
senses.example: The origination of the signal was traced to a tower on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 信号的发源地被追溯到海岸上的一座塔。
senses.why: If -ion names an action, it can also name the point where that action happened once and for all.
senses.whyCN: 既然 -ion 命名一个动作，它也能命名这个动作一劳永逸发生过的那一点。

senses.title: Financial origination
senses.definition: the process of preparing and issuing a loan or mortgage
senses.definitionCN: 准备并发放贷款或按揭的流程
senses.example: Loan origination takes several weeks before the money is released.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款发放要经过几周，资金才会放出来。
senses.why: A loan is brought into existence by a lender, so the technical term for creating it reuses the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 贷款是由放贷方「使其实有」的，所以描述这一创造过程的技术术语就沿用了同一个名词。

senses.title: The origin of life
senses.definition: in biology, the process by which life, a species, or a structure first appeared
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指生命、物种或结构最初出现的过程
senses.example: The origination of new species is explained by natural selection.
senses.exampleCN: 新物种的起源由自然选择来解释。
senses.why: Science asks not only where things begin but how the beginning itself works, and turns the act into a study.
senses.whyCN: 科学不只问事物从何处开始，还问「开始」本身如何发生，于是把这个动作变成了研究课题。

intro.en: Origination is the Latin-derived verb originate plus the noun suffix -ion, built on origo, a source or rising.
intro.cn: origination 由拉丁系动词 originate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，词根是 origo（源头、涌出）。

items.en: Oriri means to rise, and the image is water or light coming up from a source.
items.cn: oriri 意为升起，意象是水或光从源头处涌上来。

items.en: Origo names the source itself, including descent and family line.
items.cn: origo 指源头本身，也包括出身与家世。

items.en: French originer supplies the verb pattern that English later extended.
items.cn: 法语 originer 提供了英语后来扩展的动词模式。

items.en: The verb originate appears in the seventeenth century; origination is formed on its model with -ion.
items.cn: 动词 originate 见于十七世纪；origination 则仿照它加 -ion 构成。

items.en: Finance and biology adopted origination as a technical label for creating loans and for the appearance of new forms of life.
items.cn: 金融与生物学把 origination 用作技术标签，分别指放贷与新生命形态的出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same source family; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns for beginnings, each with a different flavour.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「源头」词族；近义组收其他表示开始的名词，各自意味不同。

entries.definition: to begin to exist or to create something
the person who first thought of or made something
the quality of being new and different
the act of making something completely new
entries.definitionCN: 创造；创建，强调完全新造。

entries.definition: the formal beginning of an organisation or project
entries.definitionCN: 机构或计划的正式开端。

entries.definition: the first part or point of something, the plain everyday word
entries.definitionCN: 开头；起点，最普通的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real source root and the noun patterns that origination actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「源头」词根，以及 origination 实际出现的名词搭配。

normal.en: Origination is originate plus -ion: the same action turned into a name.
normal.cn: origination 是 originate 加 -ion：把同一个动作变成名词。

normal.en: Origo is the spring and origination is the act of springing, so the noun names the motion, not the water.
normal.cn: origo 是泉眼，origination 是涌出这个动作，所以这个名词命名的是动作而不是水。

normal.en: Banks talk about loan origination, meaning the whole process of setting up a loan.
normal.cn: 银行说 loan origination，指的是把一笔贷款办成发放的整个流程。

normal.en: Originator is the person, origination is the deed, and origin is the place it all came from.
normal.cn: originator 是人，origination 是行为，origin 是这一切来的地方。

normal.en: Like orientation, the -tion ending gives this word an abstract, noun-like feel.
normal.cn: 和 orientation 一样，-tion 结尾让这个词带上抽象名词的味道。

abstract.en: Imagine holding a cup under a spring: the moment the first water falls in is the origination.
abstract.cn: 想象把一只杯子放到泉眼下面：第一滴水落进杯中的那一刻，就是 origination。

abstract.en: Think of a business plan stamped with a single date: that stamp marks its origination.
abstract.cn: 想象一份商业计划上盖了一个唯一的日期：那个日期标出了它的创始。

abstract.en: Ask not only where the river comes from but how it first began to flow, and you are asking about origination.
abstract.cn: 不只问这条河从哪里来，还问它最初怎样开始流动，你问的就是 origination。

examples.en: The origination of the festival is still a mystery to historians.
examples.cn: 这个节日的起源对历史学家来说仍是个谜。

examples.en: Loan origination costs have risen sharply this year.
examples.cn: 今年的贷款发放成本大幅上升。

examples.en: Her book traces the origination of the modern novel.
examples.cn: 她的书追溯了现代小说的起源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，瑞珍，内申」——瑞珍从泉眼取出第一捧水，写下「创始记录」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 oriri（升起；涌出）→ origo（源头；出身）→ 动词 originate + 名词后缀 -ion → origination，核心义「涌出、开始存在的这件事」。

sensesIntro.en: Origination names the springing up itself: the fact of beginning, the act of creating, the point it came from, and the technical label for loans and for new species.
sensesIntro.cn: origination 命名「涌出」本身：开始这一事实、创造这个行为、它所来自的那一点，以及放贷与新物种这类技术标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand cupping the first water that leaves a spring.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从泉眼处捧起第一捧流出的水。

branches.en: The factual branch: the fact that something began.
branches.cn: 事实分支：某事物开始这一事实。

branches.en: The creative branch: a person deliberately brings something into being.
branches.cn: 创造分支：有意识地使某物存在。

branches.en: The locative branch: the place or moment the beginning came from.
branches.cn: 定位分支：开始发生的地点或时刻。

branches.en: The financial branch: making a loan exists as a named process.
branches.cn: 金融分支：把办理贷款当作一个有名称的流程。

branches.en: The biological branch: the beginning of life and its forms becomes a subject of study.
branches.cn: 生物分支：生命及其形态的开始成为研究课题。

definition_zh: 装饰性的；观赏性的；起装饰作用的；（植物）观赏的
definition_en: used for decoration or adding beauty rather than for practical use
core_image: 一面挂满雕花铜镜和金漆画框的墙，镜子照不出人，画框里也只是一块空布
scene: 客厅墙上挂着一面华丽却照不清人的镜子。The mirror on the living room wall is ornamental rather than useful.
sceneCN: 这里 ornamental 是「装饰性的」（第 1 个义项：只为好看、不讲究实用）；句意：客厅墙上那面镜子是装饰性的，并不实用。

pos.zh: 装饰品；观赏植物（常用复数 ornamentals）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 ornamentum 直接借入，义为「装饰品；装饰」
ornament 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「装饰（总称）；纹饰」
ornament 加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，义为「有装饰的」
ornamented 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「素面无装饰的」
ornamental 加 -ist 构成，义为「专做装饰的工匠或画师」

senses.title: Serving only as decoration
senses.definition: existing to make something look attractive rather than to do a job
senses.definitionCN: 为了让人或物好看而存在，而不是为了发挥功能
senses.example: The handles on those old drawers are purely ornamental.
senses.exampleCN: 那些旧抽屉上的拉手纯粹是装饰。
senses.why: The root ornamentum means an adornment, and the -al suffix makes it a quality, so the word names the look of a thing rather than its use.
senses.whyCN: 词根 ornamentum 意为「装饰物」，加上形容词后缀 -al 表示性质，所以这个词描述的是外观而非用途。

senses.title: Kept for its appearance
senses.definition: grown or kept so that people can look at and enjoy it, not for food or work
senses.definitionCN: 为了供人观赏、欣赏而种植或饲养，而不是为了食用或干活
senses.example: Farmers turned the old paddies into ornamental ponds for carp.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把旧稻田改成观赏锦鲤池。
senses.why: Once a plant or animal is kept for beauty alone, the same decorative idea moves from objects to living things.
senses.whyCN: 当动植物只为美观而饲养种植时，「装饰、好看」的意象就从物品延伸到了活物身上。

senses.title: Fancy in style, short on function
senses.definition: elaborate and attractive in style but not practical or necessary
senses.definitionCN: 样式繁复好看，却不实用也不必需
senses.example: Critics called the new station ornamental architecture with no trains to serve.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这座新车站是华而不实的建筑，根本没有列车可服务。
senses.why: If decoration is all a thing has, its beauty becomes the whole of it, so the word shades into a comment on waste.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个东西只剩下装饰，美就成了它的全部，于是这个词也带上「浪费、多余」的评说意味。

senses.title: Decorative ornaments in the plural
senses.titleCN: 装饰品；观赏植物（复数名词）
senses.definition: objects or plants bought and placed for decoration, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 买来摆放以作装饰的物品或植物，常用复数形式
senses.example: The market sells garden ornamentals in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春季市场上出售园艺观赏植物。
senses.why: English often turns a Latin adjective into a noun with -s, so what is ornamental becomes the ornamentals themselves.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把拉丁形容词复数化当名词用，于是「装饰性的（东西）」就成了「装饰品、观赏植物」这些实物的统称。

senses.title: Decoration that adds grace
senses.definition: adding grace or charm to something without changing what it is
senses.definitionCN: 为某物增添优雅或魅力，却不改变它本身的性质
senses.example: A row of ornamental trees softened the edge of the car park.
senses.exampleCN: 一排点景树让停车场的边缘柔和了许多。
senses.why: Ornament comes from a verb meaning to equip or adorn, so a light touch of beauty can be added without strengthening the structure.
senses.whyCN: ornament 源于一个意为「配备、点缀」的动词，所以可以只加一点美而不加固结构，这就是点缀义。

intro.en: Ornamental goes back to Latin ornamentum, a decoration, from ornare, to equip or adorn, through French ornemental.
intro.cn: ornamental 源自拉丁语 ornamentum（装饰物），源于 ornare（配备、装饰），经法语 ornemental 进入英语。

items.en: Ornare means to equip, fit out, or adorn, and ornatum is its past participle.
items.cn: ornare 意为配备、装备或装饰，ornatum 是它的过去分词。

items.en: Ornamentum names a thing that adorns, an ornament or an honour.
items.cn: ornamentum 指用来装饰的东西，即装饰品或荣耀。

items.en: Ornement carries the noun into French, and ornemental adds the adjective.
items.cn: ornement 把名词带入法语，ornemental 则构成其形容词。

items.en: Ornament appears in English in the thirteenth century for decoration.
items.cn: ornament 于十三世纪进入英语，指装饰。

items.en: Ornamental is recorded from the seventeenth century and spreads to gardens and architecture.
items.cn: ornamental 于十七世纪见于记录，并扩展到园艺与建筑领域。

note.en: Ornamental belongs to the ornare family of adorning words, and sits beside everyday words for decoration and beauty.
note.cn: ornamental 属于 ornare「装饰」词族，与日常常见的装饰、美观类词相邻。

entries.definition: a decorative object
decoration added to something
richly decorated
made to look good rather than to be useful
affecting only the surface appearance
designed for practical use

normalIntro.en: Ornamental borrows the whole ornare family: adorning something, being an adornment, or being richly decorated are all part of one idea.
normalIntro.cn: ornamental 借用了整个 ornare 词族：装饰某物、作为装饰品、被装饰得华丽，都出自同一个念头。

normal.en: Purely ornamental means it has no job except to be looked at.
normal.cn: purely ornamental 表示它除了给人看没有别的作用。

normal.en: An ornamental garden is planted for beauty, not for vegetables.
normal.cn: an ornamental garden 是种来好看的园子，不是为了收菜。

normal.en: The same root gives ornament and ornate, so an ornate hall is a hall full of ornament.
normal.cn: 同根词还有 ornament 与 ornate，所以 ornate hall 就是装饰满然的厅堂。

normal.en: In biology, ornamental features attract mates the way jewellery catches the eye.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，ornamental 特征吸引配偶，就像珠宝吸引目光一样。

normal.en: As a noun it takes -s: nurseries sell ornamentals for the border.
normal.cn: 作名词时用复数形式：苗圃出售用于花境边缘的观赏植物。

abstract.en: Picture a gilded picture frame hung on a wall with nothing painted inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙挂着鎏金的画框，框里却没有画。

abstract.en: Imagine a peacock spreading its tail while the plain hens forage.
abstract.cn: 想象孔雀开屏炫耀，而朴素的母鸡在旁边觅食。

abstract.en: Think of a vase shaped like a swan that cannot hold water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只天鹅造型的花瓶，却根本装不住水。

examples.en: These shrubs are ornamental and bear no fruit.
examples.cn: 这些灌木是观赏性的，不结果实。

examples.en: The arch has ornamental value but now supports nothing.
examples.cn: 这座拱门有装饰价值，如今却不承重。

examples.en: Gardeners warn that some ornamentals spread very quickly.
examples.cn: 园丁提醒说，有些观赏植物蔓延得极快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，那门头」——门口那串「哦，那门头」的挂饰只是看着好看，这就是 ornamental 装饰性的；纯属拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ornare（配备、装饰）→ ornamentum（装饰物）→ 古法语 ornement／ornemental → 英语 ornament、ornamental，核心义「为好看而加的装饰」。

sensesIntro.en: Ornamental starts from anything that decorates an object, moves to plants and animals kept for their looks, then to an unflattering comment on things that work only as decoration.
sensesIntro.cn: ornamental 从「给物品加装饰的」出发，延伸到「为观赏而种养的」，再带出「只作装饰、不实用」的贬义评说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shining frame around an empty picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：华丽画框围着的一幅空画。

branches.en: An object that adds beauty is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 能增添美感的物件是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Plants and fish kept for looks extend beauty to living things.
branches.cn: 为观赏而种养的植物与鱼，把「美」延伸到活物。

branches.en: Beauty with no use becomes the critical sense.
branches.cn: 只有美而无用途，便成为带批评色彩的义项。

branches.en: Plural nouns for ornaments and ornamental plants grow from the same adjective.
branches.cn: 装饰品与观赏植物的复数名词义，也由同一形容词长成。

branches.en: A light touch of grace and a purely decorative piece share the adorning root.
branches.cn: 轻巧点缀与纯粹装饰品共享「装饰」这一词根。

intro.en: Ornamental is an -al adjective on the Latin stem ornare, so its family includes ornate, ornamentation, and the verb ornament.
intro.cn: ornamental 是加在拉丁词干 ornare 上的 -al 形容词，同族还包括 ornate、ornamentation 以及动词 ornament。

latinIntro.en: Latin ornare means to equip or adorn, ornamentum means an ornament, and -al marks the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ornare 意为配备或装饰，ornamentum 意为装饰物，-al 则标示形容词。

items.example: Ornare gives the idea of dressing a thing up.
items.exampleCN: ornare 提供「给某物配上装饰」的意思。

items.example: Ornamentum is the direct source of ornament.
items.exampleCN: ornamentum 是 ornament 的直接来源。

items.meaning: relating to, of the nature of
items.example: The suffix -al turns ornament into ornamental.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把 ornament 变成 ornamental。

items.example: Ornamental describes anything kept for beauty.
items.exampleCN: ornamental 描述一切为美观而保留的东西。

items.example: Bells and ribbons ornament the tree.
items.exampleCN: 铃铛和丝带装饰着这棵树。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation gives ornamentation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 ornamentation。

items.example: Baroque churches are famous for heavy ornamentation.
items.exampleCN: 巴洛克教堂以繁复用纹饰闻名。

items.example: Ornate keeps the past participle of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: ornate 保留了拉丁动词的过去分词形式。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unornamented.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unornamented。

items.example: Ornamented walls keep the past participle.
items.exampleCN: ornamented 保留了动词的过去分词形态。

definition_zh: 鸵鸟；（引申）把头埋进沙子里逃避现实的人；否认现实的做法
definition_en: a very large African bird that cannot fly and runs on long legs, or someone who refuses to face a problem
core_image: 一只背着小山般双腿的大鸟在草原上飞奔，长长的脖子压成一条线向前指
scene: 鸵鸟遇险时会贴地伏下，把头颈藏到地面上。An ostrich can sprint at seventy kilometres an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 ostrich 是「鸵鸟」（第 1 个义项：非洲大型不会飞的鸟）；句意：鸵鸟冲刺速度可达每小时七十公里。

collocations.zh: 鸵鸟政策；掩耳盗铃的做法

collocations.phrase: bury your head in the sand like an ostrich
collocations.zh: 像鸵鸟一样把头埋进沙子

derivatives.zh: ostrich 加后缀 -like 构成，义为「鸵鸟似的；逃避现实的」
ostrich 加抽象名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「鸵鸟心态；自欺」

senses.title: The large running bird
senses.definition: a tall African bird with a long neck and strong legs that runs fast but cannot fly
senses.definitionCN: 一种高大、长颈、腿脚有力的非洲鸟类，跑得很快却不会飞
senses.example: A pair of ostriches paced along the fence of the reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 两只鸵鸟沿着保护区的围栏踱步。
senses.why: The medieval name said plainly that this was a big sparrow-like bird, and centuries of trade and farming kept that picture of a giant bird alive.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的名称直白地说它是「大麻雀」，数百年的贸易与养殖让这幅大鸟图景一直保留下来。

senses.title: A person who will not look
senses.definition: someone who refuses to see or deal with an obvious danger or problem
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝看清或处理显而易见的危险与问题的人
senses.example: Calling them ostriches will not fix the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 骂他们逃避现实解决不了预算问题。
senses.why: The old tale of the bird hiding its head made the animal a ready picture for anyone who shuts their eyes to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 鸵鸟藏头的古老说法让这种鸟成了「对麻烦闭上眼睛的人」的现成比喻。

senses.title: The habit of refusing to face facts
senses.titleCN: 鸵鸟心态；掩耳盗铃的做法
senses.definition: a policy or attitude that denies a problem instead of addressing it
senses.definitionCN: 否认问题而不去解决的政策或态度
senses.example: Their ostrich approach to the leak only made the loss worse.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对泄漏采取鸵鸟式态度，结果损失更大。
senses.why: As an adjective the bird name labels a whole way of behaving, not just one person.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个鸟名标注的是整套行为方式，而不只是某一个人。

senses.title: The bird as a farm animal
senses.definition: ostriches kept on farms for meat, leather, and feathers
senses.definitionCN: 在农场中为肉、皮和羽毛而饲养的鸵鸟
senses.example: The region now runs one of the largest ostrich farms in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区现在经营着世界上最大的鸵鸟养殖场之一。
senses.why: Nineteenth century fashion for plumes and later leatherwork turned a wild bird into farm stock.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪对羽毛饰品的追捧以及后来的皮革加工，把野鸟变成了农场的牲畜。

intro.en: Ostrich comes through Old French from Latin avis struthio, a large sparrow, reshaped in English by folk etymology to end in -ish.
intro.cn: ostrich 经古法语来自拉丁语 avis struthio（「大麻雀」），英语中受民间词源影响改写成以 -ish 收尾。

items.en: Greek strouthos means a sparrow, and megas means great, so megas strouthos was the great sparrow.
items.cn: 希腊语 strouthos 意为麻雀，megas 意为大，因此 megas strouthos 就是「大麻雀」。

items.en: Latin borrowed this as avis struthio or struthiocamelus, the sparrow camel, a name that shows confusion about an unknown bird.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 avis struthio 或 struthiocamelus（「麻雀骆驼」），可见当时对这种陌生鸟儿的分辨不清。

items.en: Old French has ostruce, where a final letter disappeared from the Latin ending.
items.cn: 古法语作 ostruce，拉丁词尾在其中丢了一个音。

items.en: Middle English writers spell it ostriche or ostrige, and the -ch was probably influenced by bird.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 ostriche 或 ostrige，结尾的 -ch 可能受到 bird 的影响。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the sense of a person who ignores trouble grows from an ancient tale of the bird.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，由一则关于这种鸟的古老传说衍生出「逃避现实的人」这一比喻义。

note.en: Ostrich is a borrowed bird name with no live Latin root in English, so its look-alikes are other big flightless birds and its near meanings are the words for refusing to see.
note.cn: ostrich 是借入的鸟名，英语中没有活的拉丁词根，因此形近词是其他不会飞的大鸟，而近义词是「拒绝看清」一类的词。

entries.definition: a large flightless bird of Australia
entries.definitionCN: 原产澳大利亚的大型不会飞的鸟

entries.definition: a large flightless bird of South America
entries.definitionCN: 原产南美的大型不会飞的鸟

entries.definition: a seabird that swims instead of flying
entries.definitionCN: 以游泳代替飞行的海鸟

entries.definition: a refusal to accept that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝接受某事属实的心理状态

entries.definition: the act of avoiding something unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 回避不愉快之事的行为

entries.definition: believing something because you want it to be true

normalIntro.en: Ostrich is mostly a borrowed German bird name, and two plain facts about the bird carry the word: it cannot fly, and it is said to hide its head.
normalIntro.cn: ostrich 主要是从日耳曼语借来的鸟名，词义靠两个简单事实撑起：它不会飞，传说它会把头藏起来。

normal.en: The plural is ostriches, adding -es after the ch sound.
normal.cn: 复数是 ostriches，因为在 ch 音后加 -es。

normal.en: Ostrich egg is the largest egg of any living bird.
normal.cn: ostrich egg 是所有现存鸟类中最大的蛋。

normal.en: Ostrich feathers were once the centre of the plume trade.
normal.cn: ostrich feathers 曾经是羽毛饰品贸易的核心。

normal.en: An ostrich policy means pretending a problem does not exist.
normal.cn: an ostrich policy 指假装问题不存在。

normal.en: The German Straus and English stray are close in form, but the bird name has a different origin.
normal.cn: 德语 Straus 与英语 stray 形式相近，但鸟名的来源并不相同。

abstract.en: Picture a bird as tall as a doorway with emu-like grey feathers and enormous legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只高及门框的鸟，灰扑扑的羽毛，腿却粗壮惊人。

abstract.en: Imagine the long neck jerking forward and back like a pump handle as it runs.
abstract.cn: 想象它奔跑时长长的脖子像泵柄一样前后摆动。

abstract.en: See a person standing in a desert with sand over their eyes and ears still listening.
abstract.cn: 想想一个站在沙漠里的人，沙子盖住眼睛，耳朵却还在听。

examples.en: Ostriches can outrun most horses over short distances.
examples.cn: 鸵鸟在短距离内能跑过大多数马。

examples.en: The company kept an ostrich view of its falling sales.
examples.cn: 公司对下滑的销量抱持一种鸵鸟式的看法。

examples.en: Two ostriches were feeding beside the road.
examples.cn: 两只鸵鸟在路边觅食。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，是他去」——「哦，是他去」沙漠里把自己藏起来的，就是那只把头埋进沙子的 ostrich；这纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 strouthos（麻雀）＋ megas（大）→ 拉丁语 avis struthio（大麻雀）→ 古法语 ostruce → 英语 ostrich，词根只意味着「一种大鸟」，比喻义「逃避现实」来自民间传说。

sensesIntro.en: Ostrich begins as the name of one giant flightless bird and then widens into a label for anyone who refuses to face a visible problem.
sensesIntro.cn: ostrich 起初只是一种巨大的不会飞的鸟的名字，后来扩展为「拒绝面对明显问题的人」的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant bird sprinting with its neck stretched flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只巨鸟伸平脖子飞奔。

branches.en: The animal sense is the base of everything else.
branches.cn: 动物义是一切引申的基础。

branches.en: The head-in-sand tale turns the bird into a type of person.
branches.cn: 藏头的传说把鸟变成了某类人的典型。

branches.en: As an adjective the bird name labels a whole policy.
branches.cn: 作形容词时，这个鸟名标注的是一整套做法。

branches.en: Farms keep the real animal in daily use.
branches.cn: 养殖场让真实的鸟仍在日常使用中出现。

branches.en: A person and a policy share the same refusal to look.
branches.cn: 人和政策共享同一种「不肯看」的态度。

intro.en: Ostrich is not built from English affixes; it is a borrowed noun whose shape comes from Latin and French, with only -es joining it as a plural.
intro.cn: ostrich 不是由英语词缀构成的，而是借来的名词，其形态来自拉丁语与法语，只有复数词尾 -es 与它相连。

latinIntro.en: Latin avis struthio joins a bird word to Greek strouthos, a sparrow, giving the sense of a great sparrow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 avis struthio 把「鸟」与希腊语 strouthos（麻雀）连在一起，意为「大麻雀」。

items.example: Strouthos is the small bird the big one was compared with.
items.exampleCN: strouthos 是被比作的那只小鸟。

items.example: Megas strouthos means great sparrow.
items.exampleCN: megas strouthos 意为大麻雀。

items.example: Struthio is the Latin name of the bird.
items.exampleCN: struthio 是这种鸟的拉丁名。

items.example: Avis struthio literally says bird ostrich.
items.exampleCN: avis struthio 字面就是「鸵鸟之鸟」。

items.example: Struthiocamelus shows the old confusion about the bird.
items.exampleCN: struthiocamelus 显示出古人对这种鸟的误解。

items.example: Ostruche is the French form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: ostruche 是英语借入时的法语形态。

items.example: Ostrige is an early English spelling.
items.exampleCN: ostrige 是早期英语的一种拼法。

items.example: The suffix -es gives ostriches.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -es 构成 ostriches。

items.example: The suffix -like gives ostrich-like.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -like 构成 ostrich-like。

items.example: Ostrichism names a whole policy of denial.
items.exampleCN: ostrichism 指整套否认现实的做法。

definition_zh: 爆发；突然发生；（疾病、战争、火灾等的）爆发；暴发；疫情
definition_en: a sudden start of something harmful, such as a disease, a war, or violence
core_image: 皮下压了很久的一股热气突然冲破皮肤，红了、肿了、冒了出来
scene: 夏令营里接连有孩子发烧起疹子。A measles outbreak closed the summer camp for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 outbreak 是「（疾病的）爆发」（第 1 个义项：疾病突然流行）；句意：一场麻疹疫情让夏令营停办了一周。

pos.zh: 爆发；暴发；突然发生；疫情

derivatives.zh: outbreak 的组成部分，义为「破裂；冲破」，爆发义由此而来
与 outbreak 同用 break 加 out 构词，但指「越狱；突围；突破」，义为「逃出」
outbreak 加后缀 -related 构成的复合形容词，义为「与疫情暴发有关的」

senses.title: A disease spreading suddenly
senses.definition: a sudden appearance and spread of a disease among people or animals
senses.definitionCN: 疾病在人群或动物中突然出现并扩散
senses.example: The hospital reported an outbreak of flu among the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 医院报告员工中暴发流感。
senses.why: Disease that was hidden suddenly breaks out into view, and the word keeps that image of something pressing through.
senses.whyCN: 潜伏的疾病突然冲破皮肤般显露出来，这个词就保留了「压不住、冒出来」的意象。

senses.title: The start of war or fighting
senses.definition: the sudden beginning of war, fighting, or armed conflict
senses.definitionCN: 战争、斗殴或武装冲突的突然开始
senses.example: Many families fled at the outbreak of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家庭在战争爆发时逃离。
senses.why: Violence held in check for years breaks out in one moment, exactly like an eruption through a hard surface.
senses.whyCN: 被压抑多年的暴力在一个瞬间冲破束缚，和冲破硬表面一样，正是爆发的意思。

senses.title: A sudden rush of anger or violence
senses.titleCN: （愤怒、暴力等情绪的）突然爆发
senses.definition: a sudden burst of strong feeling or of unrestrained violent action
senses.definitionCN: 强烈情绪或不受约束的暴力行为的突然迸发
senses.example: Shops shut early after an outbreak of looting.
senses.exampleCN: 抢劫事件爆发后，商店纷纷提前关门。
senses.why: Feelings and crowds can also push out of their usual limits, so the word marks a burst rather than a cause.
senses.whyCN: 情绪与人群也会越出平常的限度，所以这个词只标出「迸发」而不追问原因。

senses.title: A mass appearance of pests or fire
senses.definition: a sudden mass appearance of insects, pests, or fire across a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫、害虫或火灾在大片区域内突然成批出现
senses.example: Farmers faced an outbreak of locusts after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨之后农民面对大规模的蝗虫爆发。
senses.why: Any natural force that lies low and then floods an area can break out of its usual bounds.
senses.whyCN: 任何潜伏之后又铺满一地的自然力量，都能越出常界，所以害虫火灾都用这个词。

senses.title: An outbreak in medicine
senses.definition: a sudden appearance of a rash or of symptoms on the body
senses.definitionCN: 皮疹或身体症状的突然出现
senses.example: The doctor asked when the outbreak on her arms first appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问她手臂上的疹子是什么时候冒出来的。
senses.why: In daily medical speech the same image is fully literal: a red patch breaks out through the skin.
senses.whyCN: 在日常医疗说法中，这个意象近乎字面：一片红疹就是「冲破皮肤」冒出来的。

intro.en: Outbreak is an English compound of out and break, first meaning a breaking out of any sort, then fixed to disease and war.
intro.cn: outbreak 是英语用 out 与 break 合成的复合词，最初指任何「破出」，后来固定用于疾病与战争。

items.en: The verbs brecan, to break, and ut, out, are both native words, so the parts of the compound are ancient.
items.cn: 动词 brecan（破裂）与 ut（向外）都是本族词，故复合词的部件十分古老。

items.en: Recorded break-out spells first describe a prisoner escaping or a siege being broken.
items.cn: 早期记录的 break-out 多指囚犯脱逃或围城被冲破。

items.en: Outbreak is used for the sudden start of disease, war, or riot in the early modern period.
items.cn: 近现代早期，outbreak 开始用于疾病、战争或暴乱的突发。

items.en: Outbreak of war becomes a fixed phrase in the age of mass armies and newspapers.
items.cn: 在大军与报纸的时代，爆发战争的说法成为固定搭配。

items.en: Public health gives the word a technical sense, an outbreak being a case count above the expected level.
items.cn: 公共卫生领域赋予其技术含义：病例数超出预期水平即为一次暴发。

note.en: Outbreak is a compound whose second half, break, carries the burst image, so its look-alikes are the other break compounds and its near meanings are the sudden-start words.
note.cn: outbreak 的爆发意象压在后半部分 break 上，因此形近词是其他以 break 构成的复合词，近义词则是表示突发起始的词。

entries.definition: an escape or a sudden success
entries.definitionCN: 越狱；突围；也指突然成功，与 outbreak 词序相反、含义不同

entries.definition: a sudden release of strong feeling
a failure of a machine or a person
a disease spreading quickly in a community
entries.definitionCN: 在社区中迅速传播的流行病

entries.definition: a violent bursting out of a volcano or of trouble
entries.definitionCN: 火山或事端的猛烈爆发

entries.definition: a sudden short burst of illness or anger
entries.definitionCN: 病情或怒气的短暂骤然发作

normalIntro.en: Outbreak says what it shows: something kept inside finally breaks out.
normalIntro.cn: outbreak 一词见字如面：被压在里面的东西终于破出。

normal.en: Break is the root, so the word pictures a bursting through.
normal.cn: break 是词根，所以这个词画的是「冲破而出」。

normal.en: Out points the direction: from inside to open view, or across a whole region.
normal.cn: out 指明方向：从内部走到明处，或铺展到整片区域。

normal.en: Compare breakthrough and outbreak: one breaks through a barrier, the other breaks out of control.
normal.cn: 对比 breakthrough 与 outbreak：前者冲破障碍，后者冲破控制。

normal.en: Disease outbreak and outbreak of war are the two fixed pairs.
normal.cn: disease outbreak 与 outbreak of war 是最固定的两类搭配。

normal.en: Uncountable events use the phrase: at the outbreak of the fighting.
normal.cn: 不可数式的事件常用短语「at the outbreak of the fighting」。

abstract.en: Picture a boil that swells under the skin and finally bursts through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗脓包在皮下鼓起，终于破皮而出。

abstract.en: See a crowd in one street that suddenly fills every side street at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上的人群瞬间灌满所有小巷。

abstract.en: Think of a lid pressed down on a boiling pot for years, then flung off.
abstract.cn: 想象锅盖压了多年，最后被蒸气掀飞。

examples.en: Health teams rushed to the village to contain the outbreak.
examples.cn: 医疗队迅速赶到村里控制疫情。

examples.en: The outbreak of war halted the project.
examples.cn: 战争的爆发使项目中止。

examples.en: Doctors reported the first outbreaks in the north early that winter.
examples.cn: 那年入冬不久，医生就报告了北部最早的几次疫情暴发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特不累克」——奥特英雄冲出来打破包围、一点也不累，就是 outbreak 的「冲破而出」；只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本族词 out（向外）＋ break（破裂）→ outbreak（破出、爆发）；与拉丁语无直接联系，形象来自「从内部冲破」这一动作。

sensesIntro.en: Outbreak moves from a disease bursting into view to the sudden start of war, of anger, of pests or fire, and finally to a rash on the skin.
sensesIntro.cn: outbreak 从疾病突然冒出，延伸到战争爆发、情绪迸发、虫害火灾骤起，最后落到皮肤上的疹子发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held inside bursting out and spreading.
core.cn: 核心意象：被压住的东西破皮而出、四下蔓延。

branches.en: Disease is the most common and most technical use today.
branches.cn: 疾病是今天最常见也最技术化的用法。

branches.en: War shares the sudden-start sense with disease.
branches.cn: 战争与疾病共享「突然开始」的义项。

branches.en: An outburst of feeling is the human version of the burst.
branches.cn: 情绪迸发是「冲破」在人身上的版本。

branches.en: Pests and rashes bring the image back to physical things that appear all at once.
branches.cn: 虫害与皮疹把意象带回同时出现的实体事物。

branches.en: Both a public health event and a violent crowd need the same word for sudden spread.
branches.cn: 公共卫生事件与暴力群体都需要同一个表示「骤然扩散」的词。

intro.en: Outbreak is built from two native English words rather than a Latin root, but compounds of out behave like prefixes and are learned together.
intro.cn: outbreak 由两个英语本族词构成，而非拉丁词根；但以 out 构成的复合词有类前缀的作用，宜一起记。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the nearest Latin influence is break, which is native, and the family grows from Old English brecan and ut.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；英语 break 属本族词，词族来自古英语 brecan（破裂）与 ut（向外）。

items.example: Out- often marks a movement beyond a limit.
items.exampleCN: out- 常表示越出某个限度。

items.example: Break supplies the bursting image.
items.exampleCN: break 提供「破裂」的意象。

items.example: Outbreak keeps the meaning of a break-out.
items.exampleCN: outbreak 保留了「破出」的含义。

items.example: Breakout reverses the order and moves to escape.
items.exampleCN: breakout 词序相反，义为逃出。

items.example: Outburst focuses on feeling, not disease.
items.exampleCN: outburst 侧重情绪而非疾病。

items.example: Outset shares the early-start idea.
items.exampleCN: outset 共享「起始」的概念。

items.example: Outnumber shows out- as more than.
items.exampleCN: outnumber 展示 out- 表「超过」。

items.example: Outlive shows out- as beyond in time.
items.exampleCN: outlive 展示 out- 表时间上的「超出」。

items.example: Breakdown ends in failure, not spread.
items.exampleCN: breakdown 落点是失败而非扩散。

items.example: Breakthrough breaks through a wall instead of out of control.
items.exampleCN: breakthrough 是冲破墙，而不是冲破控制。

definition_zh: 爆发；迸发；（情感的）突然发作
definition_en: a sudden, violent release of feeling or activity, often loud or angry
core_image: 闸门猛地打开，积压的水一下子冲出来
scene: 会议室里，积压已久的怨气终于有人忍不住大声说了出来。A sudden outburst of anger startled everyone in the meeting room.
sceneCN: 这里 outburst 是「（情感的）爆发」（第 1 个义项：压抑的情绪突然、猛烈地宣泄出来）；句意为突如其来的怒火让会议室里所有人都吓了一跳。

derivatives.zh: outburst 的复数形式，义为「多次爆发」
由 outburst 加 -ing 构成，义为「骤然迸发的」

senses.title: A sudden burst of emotion
senses.definition: a sudden, strong expression of a feeling, especially anger or joy
senses.definitionCN: 情感突然而强烈的表露，尤指愤怒或喜悦
senses.example: His outburst of anger shocked the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 他突如其来的怒火把全家人都震住了。
senses.why: The verb burst means to break open suddenly, and out- shows that what was held inside rushes outward, so an outburst is feeling breaking through its container.
senses.whyCN: burst 意为「突然迸裂」，out- 表示向外，被压住的东西一下子冲出来；因此 outburst 就是情感突破了它的容器。

senses.title: A sudden loud release of sound
senses.definition: a sudden short period of loud noise, laughter or activity
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂的一阵响亮声音、笑声或活动
senses.example: The crowd gave a loud outburst of applause when the singer appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手一出场，人群便爆发出一阵热烈的掌声。
senses.why: The same bursting image applies to sound, which seems to leave a quiet room all at once.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「迸裂」的意象也适用于声音：安静的房间里忽然涌出一大团响声。

senses.title: An eruption of a natural force
senses.definition: a sudden burst of energy or activity from a natural force or system
senses.definitionCN: 自然力量或系统释放出的突如其来的能量与活动
senses.example: The lake was formed by a violent outburst of melting water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖是由融水猛烈涌出而形成的。
senses.why: In geology the word names water or lava breaking through its barrier, the literal picture behind the emotional sense.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学里，这个词指水或岩浆冲破屏障；这正是情绪义项背后的字面画面。

senses.title: A separate short release
senses.definition: one single act of breaking out, counted as a short event
senses.definitionCN: 一次单独的爆发行为，被看作一个短暂事件
senses.example: The researchers recorded three outbursts of activity within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员在一小时内记录到三次突发的活动。
senses.why: The countable noun turns the process into separate episodes, which is why outbursts always come in bursts of one, two or three.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词把这一过程切分成一个个单独的小段，所以 outburst 总是以一次、两次或三次的「阵发」形式出现。

senses.title: An intense public protest
senses.definition: a sudden angry outcry by a group of people against something
senses.definitionCN: 一群人针对某事突然发出的愤怒呼声
senses.example: The new tax led to an outburst of protest across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 新税引发了全国范围的抗议浪潮。
senses.why: Anger shared by many people spreads like water bursting from one gate into the next, and the result is a public outbreak of protest.
senses.whyCN: 许多人的愤怒像水从一道闸门冲向下游一样扩散开来，于是形成公开的抗议爆发。

intro.en: Outburst joins the adverb out and the noun burst, which comes from an older burst, to break or shatter.
intro.cn: outburst 由副词「向外」的 out 与名词 burst 组合而成，而 burst 源自更早的 burst，意为「迸裂、炸开」。

items.en: The early verb burstan may refer to breaking or starting up, but its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 古英语中或已出现 burstan，可能指「破裂、突然开始」，其来源不确定。

items.en: Burst is recorded in the sense of breaking open suddenly.
items.cn: 中古英语里 burst 已有「突然裂开」的记录。

items.en: Burst is also used for a sudden onset of a feeling or action.
items.cn: 到了十五世纪，burst 又被用来指情感或行动的突然发作。

items.en: Out- is joined to burst to name something that breaks outwards.
items.cn: 十七世纪，前缀式的 out 与 burst 结合，用来指向外迸裂之物。

items.en: The noun outburst is used for sudden displays of emotion, activity or noise.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，名词 outburst 广泛用于情感、活动或声音的突然爆发。

note.en: Outburst belongs to the burst family, and it sits close to explosion and flare-up in meaning.
note.cn: outburst 属于 burst 词族，在语义上靠近「爆炸」与「骤然发作」这一类词。

normalIntro.en: Outburst is a burst that goes out: the force starts inside and shoots outwards.
normalIntro.cn: outburst 是「冲出去的 burst」：力量从内部开始，向外喷射。

normal.en: An outburst of anger means a sudden display of anger.
normal.cn: an outburst of anger 指突然爆发的怒火。

normal.en: The word is a compound of out and burst, so picture the break going outwards.
normal.cn: 这个词由 out 与 burst 复合而成，可把破裂的方向想成向外。

normal.en: Outbursts is simply the plural: repeated short bursts.
normal.cn: outbursts 只是复数形式，表示一次次短促的爆发。

normal.en: An outburst of laughter is a shared burst of sound.
normal.cn: an outburst of laughter 是一阵爆发出的笑声。

normal.en: Compare outbreak: an outbreak is often of disease or war, an outburst is usually of feeling.
normal.cn: 对比 outbreak：outbreak 多指疾病或战争，outburst 多指情感。

abstract.en: Imagine a pressure cooker letting out a loud whistle, then falling quiet again.
abstract.cn: 想象高压锅突然长鸣一声，随后又归于安静。

abstract.en: Picture a dam gate swinging open for one second and shut again.
abstract.cn: 想象水坝的闸门打开一秒又立刻关上。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp that flares once in the dark and then dims.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中的灯忽然一亮又暗下去。

examples.en: Her outburst at the meeting came as a complete surprise.
examples.cn: 她在会上的爆发让人完全意想不到。

examples.en: The cheerful outburst of the children in the yard woke the neighbours.
examples.cn: 院子里孩子们欢快的一阵喧闹吵醒了邻居。

examples.en: An outburst of applause followed the final speech.
examples.cn: 最后的演讲结束后响起一阵热烈的掌声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特 burst」——奥特曼一出场，burst 一声炸开，情绪冲出来；这只是谐音拆词，与词源无关。

root: 英语 out（向外）+ burst（迸裂，源自古英语 burstan）→ outburst，核心义「憋着的东西向外面迸开」。

sensesIntro.en: Outburst starts with an emotional release, extends to sounds and natural eruptions, can be counted as single episodes, and finally names shared public protest.
sensesIntro.cn: outburst 先指情感的宣泄，再扩展到声音与自然力量的迸发，又可计数为一次次单独的事件，最后指众人共同的公开抗议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate opening and held-back water rushing out.
core.cn: 核心意象：闸门打开，积压的水冲了出来。

branches.en: A sudden burst of feeling is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 情感的突然爆发是日常义项。

branches.en: Sound bursting into a quiet room is the volume sense.
branches.cn: 声音冲进安静房间是声音义项。

branches.en: A natural force breaking its barrier is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 自然力量冲破屏障是物理义项。

branches.en: Counting the bursts turns the event into separate episodes.
branches.cn: 把爆发计次，使事件成为一个个单独的片段。

branches.en: Many angry people sharing a burst of feeling produce a public protest.
branches.cn: 许多愤怒的人共享一次情感爆发，便形成公开抗议。

intro.en: Outburst is a compound of out and burst, with the related compound outbreak and the family of burst, burst out and bursting.
intro.cn: outburst 是 out 与 burst 的复合词，与之相关的是同构的 outbreak，以及 burst、outbursts 等词族成员。

latinIntro.en: Outburst has no Latin ancestor: both parts are native English, so there are no Latin relatives to list.
latinIntro.cn: outburst 没有拉丁语祖先，两部分都是英语本土词，所以没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.exampleCN: out 标明爆发向外。

items.example: Burst supplies the breaking image.
items.exampleCN: burst 提供「迸裂」的意象。

items.example: The noun burst is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 名词 burst 是复合词的后半段。

items.example: Outburst is used for feeling that breaks out.
items.exampleCN: outburst 用于冲破而出。

items.meaning: several sudden starts of something bad
items.example: Outbreaks is the plural of outbreak, a parallel compound.
items.exampleCN: outbreaks 是并列复合词 outbreak 的复数。

items.meaning: a sudden start of disease or war

items.exampleCN: outbreak 把 burst 换成 break。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成的名词词尾
