items.meaningCN: 将要迸裂的；满得要溢出的
items.example: Bursting shares the same base vowel change.
items.exampleCN: bursting 共享同一词干变化。

definition_zh: 胜过；超过；做得比……更好
definition_en: to do better than someone or something else
core_image: 两人同时起跑，一人冲过终点线才回头看对手
scene: 比赛最后一百米，落后大半程的选手突然加速，第一个冲过终点。On the final stretch she outdid every rival and crossed the line first.
sceneCN: 这里 outdo 是「胜过、做得更好」（第 1 个义项：在能力或成绩上比对手表现更出色）；句意为在最后一程她胜过所有对手，第一个冲过终点。

derivatives.zh: 由 outdo 加 -ing 构成，义为「胜过他人的行为」
outdo 的过去分词，常作表语，义为「被人比下去的」

senses.title: To do better than another
senses.definition: to perform better than another person or group in the same activity
senses.definitionCN: 在同样的活动中比另一个人或群体表现更好
senses.example: She outdid all her classmates in the speech contest.
senses.exampleCN: 她在演讲比赛中胜过了所有同学。
senses.why: Out- marks going beyond a limit and do supplies the action, so outdo means doing an action past what someone else has done.
senses.whyCN: out- 表示「越过某个界限」，do 提供动作，所以 outdo 就是把同一个动作做得超出别人。

senses.title: To surpass oneself
senses.definition: to do better than your own previous level or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 表现得超过自己过去的水平或预期
senses.example: The team outdid itself this season and reached the final.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍本赛季超水平发挥，打进了决赛。
senses.why: The same beyond-limit structure works when the opponent is your own earlier record, giving the set phrase outdo oneself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「越过界限」的结构也适用于对手是自己以往的记录，于是形成固定说法「超越自己」。

senses.title: To be more than something
senses.definition: to exceed a stated amount, degree or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 超过某个既定的数量、程度或预期
senses.example: The sales figures outdid all expectations this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的销售数字超过了所有预期。
senses.why: From a contest between people, the verb extends to any measured amount that goes beyond the expected line.
senses.whyCN: 从人与人之间的较量，这个词扩展到任何超出预期线的可测数量。

senses.title: To defeat in a contest
senses.definition: to win against or defeat an opponent in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中赢过、击败对手
senses.example: In the final round the young player outdid the champion.
senses.exampleCN: 在决赛轮里，这位年轻选手击败了冠军。
senses.why: Doing better than a competitor in a scored event naturally reads as a defeat for the other side.
senses.whyCN: 在计分的比赛中做得比对手好，自然就解读为对方输掉了比赛。

intro.en: Outdo is a native compound: the adverb out, meaning beyond, joined to the Old English verb do, to perform.
intro.cn: outdo 是英语本土复合词：副词 out 表示「超出」，与古英语动词 do（做、施行）结合而成。

items.en: Don supplies the basic verb, to do or to perform an action.
items.cn: 古英语的 don 提供基本动词，意为「做、施行」。

items.en: Ut, the ancestor of out, first means outwards, away from a place.
items.cn: out 的前身 ut 最初表示向外、离开某个地方。

items.en: Out develops the sense of going beyond a limit or standard.
items.cn: 中古英语中，out 发展出「越过界限、超过标准」的意思。

items.en: Out is attached to verbs such as do, run and shine to mean surpass.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，out 被接到 do、run、shine 等动词前，表示「胜过」。

items.en: Outdo settles as the standard verb, keeping the irregular forms outdid and outdone.
items.cn: 现代英语里 outdo 成为标准动词，并保留不规则形式 outdid 与 outdone。

note.en: Outdo has a whole family of out- verbs such as outperform, and it is close in meaning to exceed, excel and surpass.
note.cn: outdo 有一整族 out 开头的动词，如 outperform，语义上靠近「超过」「优于」这类词。

entries.definition: to run faster than someone else
to sell more than another product or company
to continue to exist longer than something else
entries.definitionCN: 比……持续得更久（out 加 last）

entries.definition: past participle of outdo, meaning surpassed
entries.definitionCN: outdo 的过去分词，意为「被比下去的」

entries.definition: to do better than another company or team
to be greater than a number or limit
to become better or greater than something else

normalIntro.en: Outdo is out plus do: you do the action past the end that the other side reached.
normalIntro.cn: outdo 就是 out 加 do：把动作做到了对方到达的终点之外。

normal.en: Out- in this family means going beyond, as in outrun and outsell.
normal.cn: 这个家族里的 out 表示「超出」，如 outrun 与 outsell。

normal.en: The verb keeps the irregular do forms: outdoes, outdid, outdone.
normal.cn: 这个动词沿用 do 的不规则变化：outdoes、outdid、outdone。

normal.en: Outdo oneself means to break your own record.
normal.cn: outdo oneself 意为打破自己的纪录。

normal.en: If you outdo a rival, the rival is beaten.
normal.cn: 如果你 outdo 了对手，对手就被击败了。

normal.en: Compare outperform, which is more common in business writing.
normal.cn: 对比 outperform，它在商务写作中更常见。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who finishes the race and looks back at the second place.
abstract.cn: 想象一位跑者冲过终点后回头看第二名。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag rising just above the red line.
abstract.cn: 想象价格标签升到红线之上一点点。

abstract.en: Imagine yourself beating the time your own clock showed last year.
abstract.cn: 想象你击败了自己去年那只表记录的时间。

examples.en: Every year the designer tries to outdo her last collection.
examples.cn: 每年这位设计师都努力超越上一次的系列。

examples.en: He outdid his brother in every subject at school.
examples.cn: 他在学校每门功课上都胜过哥哥。

examples.en: The new car outdoes its rivals on fuel economy.
examples.cn: 这款新车在燃油经济性上胜过竞争对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自豪 do」——做（do）得比谁都好，所以自豪地走到圈外；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 out（超出）+ do（做，源自古英语 don）→ outdo，核心义「把同一件事做到超出别人」。

sensesIntro.en: Outdo begins with beating a person at a task, extends to beating your own record, then to exceeding any expected amount, and finally to winning a contest outright.
sensesIntro.cn: outdo 先指在某件事上胜过别人，再扩展到超越自己的纪录、超过任何预期的数量，最后指在较量中直接取胜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one runner crossing the finish line ahead of another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名跑者在另一名跑者之前冲过终点。

branches.en: Doing an action better than another person is the central sense.
branches.cn: 把动作做得比别人好是核心义项。

branches.en: Turning the rival into your own record gives the self-bettering sense.
branches.cn: 把对手换成自己过去的纪录，便有了自我超越义项。

branches.en: Applying the verb to numbers gives the sense of exceeding an amount.
branches.cn: 把动词用于数字，便得到超过数量的义项。

branches.en: In a scored contest, doing better becomes a clear defeat for the other side.
branches.cn: 在计分比赛中，做得更好便成为对方的明确失败。

branches.en: A rival and a figure can both be outdone, which shows the beyond pattern.
branches.cn: 对手与数字都能被 outdo，正好体现「越过」的模式。

intro.en: Outdo is built from the productive prefix out-, meaning beyond, and the irregular verb do, with compounds such as outrun, outsell and outperform.
intro.cn: outdo 由能产的、表示「超出」的 out 前缀与不规则动词 do 构成，同一模式的复合词有 outrun、outsell 与 outperform。

latinIntro.en: Outdo has no Latin ancestor: both parts are native English, so there are no Latin relatives to list.
latinIntro.cn: outdo 没有拉丁语祖先，两部分都是英语本土词，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: The prefix out- means beyond a limit.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 表示超出界限。

items.example: Do supplies the core action.
items.exampleCN: do 提供核心动作。

items.example: Outdo keeps the irregular forms.
items.exampleCN: outdo 保留不规则变化。

items.example: Outdoes follows the pattern of does.
items.exampleCN: outdoes 与 does 的变化一致。

items.example: Outdid mirrors the form did.
items.exampleCN: outdid 与 did 同形变化。

items.example: Outdone mirrors the form done.
items.exampleCN: outdone 与 done 同形变化。

items.meaning: to do better in a named action
items.example: The prefix out- also forms outrun and outsell.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 还构成 outrun 与 outsell。

items.example: Outdoing works as a gerund or a noun.
items.exampleCN: outdoing 可作动名词或名词。

definition_zh: 服装；全套装备；（一个）团体；配备
definition_en: a set of clothes worn together, or the equipment or group needed for a task
core_image: 出门前把衣服与工具一件件装进同一个箱子里
scene: 行李箱摊开在床上，帽子、外套和登山鞋被一件件摆好搭配。She chose a smart outfit for the job interview.
sceneCN: 这里 outfit 是「一套服装」（第 1 个义项：搭配在一起穿的一整套衣服）；句意为她为面试挑了一套得体的衣服。

pos.zh: 一套服装；全套装备；团体；组织

derivatives.zh: 由 outfit 加 -er 构成，义为「出售服装与户外装备的商店」
由 outfit 加 -ing 构成，义为「配备、装配（过程）」
outfit 的过去分词，义为「配备了装备的」

senses.title: A set of clothes
senses.definition: a set of clothes worn together, often for a special occasion or activity
senses.definitionCN: 搭配在一起穿的一整套衣服，常用于特定场合或活动
senses.example: She wore a bright outfit to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一套鲜艳的衣服去参加聚会。
senses.why: The image of a kit assembled item by item turns into clothes that are chosen as one matched set.
senses.whyCN: 「一件件凑齐整套」的画面，落在服装上就变成被人们作为一个整体挑选的搭配。

senses.title: Equipment for a task
senses.definition: the complete set of tools or equipment needed for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所需要的成套工具或装备
senses.example: Every climber arrived with a full outfit of ropes and boots.
senses.exampleCN: 每位登山者都带来了一整套绳索和靴子。
senses.why: The original sense is a preparation for a journey, so anything assembled for a task can be an outfit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本指为远行作出的准备，所以为某项任务凑齐的任何东西都可以叫 outfit。

senses.title: To supply with equipment
senses.definition: to provide a person or group with the equipment or clothes they need
senses.definitionCN: 向某人或某群体提供所需的装备或衣服
senses.example: The school outfitted every pupil with a raincoat.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为每个学生配备了雨衣。
senses.why: Outfitting is the act behind the noun: the moment the kit is being assembled for someone.
senses.whyCN: 配备就是名词背后的动作过程：装备正在为某个人凑齐的那一刻。

senses.title: A group or company
senses.definition: a group of people working together, such as a team, band or small business
senses.definitionCN: 一起工作的一群人，如乐队、团队或小公司
senses.example: The whole outfit turned up for the rehearsal.
senses.exampleCN: 整个乐队都来参加排练了。
senses.why: A team is also a kit of people fitted together, so the informal sense names an organised group.
senses.whyCN: 一支团队也像把人们装配到一起的整套「器材」，于是这个口语义项指一个有组织的集体。

senses.title: A suit of armour
senses.definition: a complete set of armour or military dress from an earlier period
senses.definitionCN: 旧时的一整套铠甲或军装
senses.example: The museum displays an ancient outfit of chain mail.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出一套古老的锁子甲。
senses.why: In early use the equipment sense covered war gear, and armour was the ultimate matched kit.
senses.whyCN: 在早期用法中，装备义涵盖战争用具，而铠甲就是把部件配成完整一套的极致。

intro.en: Outfit is a compound of out, in its early sense of outwards or ready to start, and fit, meaning a suitable arrangement.
intro.cn: outfit 是 out 与 fit 的复合词；out 取其早期「向外、准备出发」之义，fit 表示「合适的安排」。

items.en: Fittan means to arrange or make something suitable.
items.cn: 古英语的 fittan 意为安排、使合适。

items.en: Outfit is first used for the equipment for a voyage or campaign.
items.cn: 十七世纪，outfit 最初指远航或出征所需的装备。

items.en: The word spreads to clothes worn together and to fitting out a ship.
items.cn: 十八世纪，这个词扩展到搭配成套的衣服以及为船只配备物资。

items.en: The verb outfit, to equip, becomes common alongside the noun.
items.cn: 十九世纪，动词 outfit（配备）与名词并用，变得常见。

items.en: Outfit also names any small business or organised group.
items.cn: 现代英语中，outfit 还用来指任何小公司或有组织的团体。

note.en: Outfit comes from fit, so its look-alikes include fitting and fitter, while it is close in meaning to costume and ensemble.
note.cn: outfit 源自 fit，因此形近词包括 fitting 与 fitter，语义上靠近 costume 与 ensemble。

entries.definition: a shop selling clothes and equipment
entries.definitionCN: 出售服装与装备的商店

entries.definition: a time when clothes are made to fit
a person rejected by a group
entries.definitionCN: 被排斥的人（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a factor that balances another
entries.definitionCN: 抵消因素（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: clothes worn for a role or special occasion
a set of clothes worn together
a set of tools or equipment

normalIntro.en: Outfit is fit for going out: the clothes and gear that suit you when you leave the house.
normalIntro.cn: outfit 是「出门合身的 fit」：出门时适合你的衣服和装备。

normal.en: The noun outfit keeps fit inside it, so think of clothes that fit together.
normal.cn: 名词 outfit 内含 fit，可以联想成彼此合得来的整套衣服。

normal.en: The verb outfits doubles the t: outfits, outfitted, outfitting.
normal.cn: 动词 outfit 要双写 t：outfits、outfitted、outfitting。

normal.en: Outfit someone with means to supply them with gear.
normal.cn: outfit someone with 意思是给某人配备装备。

normal.en: An outfit can also be a small company or a band.
normal.cn: outfit 也可以指一家小公司或一支乐队。

normal.en: Compare equipment: an outfit is the whole matched set, equipment is the generic term.
normal.cn: 对比 equipment：outfit 强调整套配齐，equipment 是泛指的设备。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase: one layer of clothes, one layer of tools, all fitted together.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱：一层衣服、一层工具，彼此契合地被装在一起。

abstract.en: Think of a theatre wardrobe where one costume is laid out as a whole.
abstract.cn: 想象剧院的服装间里，一套戏服从上到下被摆成一体。

abstract.en: Imagine a small band all dressed alike, standing on one stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一支小乐队穿着统一的服装，站在同一个舞台上。

examples.en: That outfit looks great on you.
examples.cn: 那套衣服穿在你身上很好看。

examples.en: The hikers were outfitted with warm jackets and strong boots.
examples.cn: 徒步者们被配发了保暖夹克和结实的靴子。

examples.en: She runs a small outfit that designs wedding dresses.
examples.cn: 她经营着一家设计婚纱的小公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特 fit」——奥特曼穿上合身的战斗服才出门，整套行头就是一套服装；这只是谐音拆词，与词源无关。

root: 英语 out（向外、准备出发）+ fit（合适、安排，古英语 fittan）→ outfit，核心义「为出门或某项事务凑齐的一整套」。

sensesIntro.en: Outfit starts as clothes worn as one set, extends to any equipment kit, then to the act of supplying it, and finally to the group that shares the kit.
sensesIntro.cn: outfit 先指成套穿着的服装，再扩展到任何成套装备，然后指配备装备的动作，最后指共享这套装备的团体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clothes and tools packed together in one case before setting out.
core.cn: 核心意象：出门前把衣服与工具一起装进同一个箱子。

branches.en: A matched set of clothes is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 配成套的衣服是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Any matched set of tools is the equipment sense.
branches.cn: 配成套的工具是装备义项。

branches.en: The act of fitting out is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 把装备配齐的动作是动词义项。

branches.en: A group of people fitted together becomes the informal group sense.
branches.cn: 被装配到一起的一群人成为口语中的团体义项。

branches.en: War gear and armour are the same matched-set idea at its oldest.
branches.cn: 战争装备与铠甲是同一「成套」观念最古老的表现。

intro.en: Outfit combines out with fit, and its family includes outfitter, outfitting and the verb forms outfit, outfitted and outfitting.
intro.cn: outfit 由 out 与 fit 组合而成，同族词包括 outfitter、outfitting，以及动词形式 outfit、outfitted 与 outfitting。

latinIntro.en: Outfit has no Latin ancestor: both parts are native English, so there are no Latin relatives to list.
latinIntro.cn: outfit 没有拉丁语祖先，两部分都是英语本土词，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Out marks setting out on a journey.
items.exampleCN: out 表示出发远行。

items.example: Fit describes a suitable arrangement.
items.exampleCN: fit 表示合适的安排。

items.example: The verb fit gives outfit its equipment sense.
items.exampleCN: 动词 fit 赋予 outfit 装备义。

items.example: Outfit names a set of clothes or gear.
items.exampleCN: outfit 指一套衣服或装备。

items.example: Outfits is the plural of the noun.
items.exampleCN: outfits 是名词的复数。

items.example: Outfitted doubles the final t.
items.exampleCN: outfitted 要双写末尾的 t。

items.example: Outfitting also names the activity.
items.exampleCN: outfitting 也指配备这项活动。

items.meaning: a person or shop that does something
items.example: The suffix -er forms outfitter.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 outfitter。

items.meaning: a shop selling clothes and equipment
items.example: Outfitter keeps the set-making idea.
items.exampleCN: outfitter 保留「配齐一套」的观念。

definition_zh: 长大而不再适合（衣物）；长大后不再有（兴趣、习惯）；长得超过（某人）；发展得使……不再适用
definition_en: to become too big or too old for something, to stop having a habit or interest, or to grow faster than someone else
core_image: 一个孩子从袖口和裤腿里钻出来，衣服被撑得绷紧
scene: 换季整理衣柜时，母亲翻出一件去年还很合身的毛衣。When she pulled the sweater over his head, she saw that he had outgrown it in a single year.
sceneCN: 这里 outgrow 是「长大而穿不下」（第 1 个义项：身体长大，衣物变得太小）；句意：当她把毛衣从他头上套下去时，发现他仅仅一年就长得穿不下了。

pos.zh: 长大而不再适合；长得超过；因成长而摆脱

collocations.zh: 长大后对某事失去兴趣

derivatives.zh: out + growth 构成，义为「自然发展的结果；长出物」，由「向外生长」引申为「衍生物」
由过去分词转类而来的形容词，义为「已长大的；不再合身的」

senses.title: To become too big for clothes
senses.definition: to grow too large to fit into a piece of clothing or a pair of shoes
senses.definitionCN: 身体长大到衣物或鞋子已经穿不下
senses.example: He outgrew his school shoes by the end of term.
senses.exampleCN: 学期末时他已经穿不下那双校鞋了。
senses.why: The prefix out- means beyond, so the body simply grows beyond the fit of the garment.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 out- 表示「超出」，身体长到了衣物尺码之外，于是「穿不下」这个义项就直接从字面组合中长出来。

senses.title: To stop having an interest or habit
senses.titleCN: 长大后不再有（兴趣、习惯）
senses.definition: to stop doing or liking something because you have become older or more mature
senses.definitionCN: 因为年龄增长或变得成熟而不再做某事、不再喜欢某事
senses.example: She outgrew her fear of the dark before she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她不到十岁就不再怕黑了。
senses.why: The same image of leaving a garment behind is applied to habits and fears that no longer fit the grown person.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「把衣服留在身后」的画面被用到了习惯与恐惧上：它们也不再适合长大了的那个人。

senses.title: To grow taller or larger than someone
senses.definition: to become taller or larger than another person, often a parent or older sibling
senses.definitionCN: 长得比另一个人更高或更大，常指超过父母或年长的兄姐
senses.example: He has finally outgrown his older brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他终于长得比哥哥高了。
senses.why: Here out- carries the sense of surpassing, so growth is measured against a rival rather than a garment.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 out- 带有「胜过」的意思，成长不再以衣服为尺子，而是与对手比较谁长得多。

senses.title: To make something no longer suitable
senses.definition: to develop so much that a plan, system, or place is no longer large or modern enough
senses.definitionCN: 发展得太快太大，使计划、制度或场所显得不够用或不够新
senses.example: The small workshop had outgrown its old building.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小工坊发展得太快，旧厂房已经不够用了。
senses.why: The metaphor shifts from a growing body to a growing organisation that bursts the container it was built for.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从长大的身体转到成长的组织：组织撑破了原本为它造好的容器，于是有了「不再适用」的意思。

intro.en: Outgrow is a native English compound of out- and grow, both Old English words, first recorded in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: outgrow 是英语本族语复合词，由古英语词 out- 与 grow 组成，首见于十七世纪。

items.en: ut- means out or beyond, and growan means to grow.
items.cn: 古英语 ut- 意为「出、在外」，growan 意为「生长」。

items.en: The two words combine in ordinary speech as out and grow.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，out 与 grow 在口语中并列使用。

items.en: Outgrow appears, first describing clothes that a child has become too big to wear.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现 outgrow，最初指孩子长大而穿不下衣服。

items.en: The word extends to habits, fears, and opinions that are left behind.
items.cn: 十九世纪词义扩展到被抛在身后的习惯、恐惧与观点。

items.en: Business and planning uses speak of a firm outgrowing its premises.
items.cn: 现代商业用法说公司发展得超出了场地规模。

note.en: Outgrow sits with its compound relatives outlast and outnumber, and with the family of grow, growth, and overgrown.
note.cn: outgrow 与同前缀复合词 outlast、outnumber 相邻，也属于 grow、growth、overgrown 这一词族。

entries.definition: to continue to exist longer than something else
to be greater in number than another group
covered with plants that have grown too much
entries.definitionCN: 长满杂草的；长得过盛的

entries.definition: to be or do better than someone or something else
to be greater than a fixed amount or limit
to go faster or become larger than someone else

normalIntro.en: Outgrow is out plus grow: you grow out of a thing until it no longer fits you.
normalIntro.cn: outgrow 就是 out 加 grow：你从某样东西里「长出去」，直到它不再合身。

normal.en: The pattern out plus a verb often means doing something beyond another person.
normal.cn: out 加动词的结构常常表示「在……方面超过别人」。

normal.en: Compare outlast and outnumber, which share the same prefix.
normal.cn: 对比 outlast 与 outnumber，它们共享同一个前缀。

normal.en: A cloud or a sound can outgrow its first shape and spread wider.
normal.cn: 云或声音可以长得超出最初的形状，向四周扩散。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in the same way as grow: grew and grown.
normal.cn: 这个动词与 grow 一样是不规则变化：grew 与 grown。

normal.en: A company often outgrows the office it started in, which is why it moves.
normal.cn: 公司常常发展得超出最初那间办公室，所以才会搬家。

abstract.en: See a child whose wrists stick out of a too-short jacket.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子的手腕从过短的夹克里露了出来。

abstract.en: Picture an old worn toy quietly left in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件旧玩具被悄悄留在抽屉里。

abstract.en: See two marks on a wall where a younger child once stood.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上留下的两道身高线，是更小的那个孩子当年站的位置。

examples.en: Children outgrow their shoes every few months.
examples.cn: 孩子们每隔几个月就长得穿不下鞋子了。

examples.en: Most teenagers outgrow their childhood fears.
examples.cn: 大多数青少年长大后不再有童年的恐惧。

examples.en: She has outgrown the town she grew up in.
examples.cn: 她已经不再适合那个她长大的小镇了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬特够」——熬到特够大了，衣服就穿不下了；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ut-（出、超出）+ growan（生长）→ 英语 out + grow → outgrow：核心义「长到了外面」，即成长超出了原有的尺码、兴趣或场所。

sensesIntro.en: Outgrow starts with clothes that no longer fit a taller body, moves to interests and fears that are left behind, then to surpassing a person and to anything that grows beyond its container.
sensesIntro.cn: outgrow 先从「身体长大、衣服穿不下」出发，再指被抛在身后的兴趣与恐惧，然后指身高超过某人，最后泛指任何成长到超出原有容器的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body bursting out of clothes that were once the right size.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体从曾经合身的衣物里撑出来。

branches.en: The most concrete branch is a child who no longer fits the garment.
branches.cn: 最具体的分支是孩子长大到衣物不再合身。

branches.en: Habits and fears are treated like old clothes that are left behind.
branches.cn: 习惯与恐惧被当作旧衣服一样留在身后。

branches.en: Growth is measured against another person instead of a garment.
branches.cn: 成长不再以衣物衡量，而是与另一个人比较。

branches.en: Organisations and plans also burst the space built for them.
branches.cn: 组织与计划也会撑破为它们准备的空间。

branches.en: Both clothes and childhood interests are things a growing person simply leaves behind.
branches.cn: 衣服与童年兴趣都是成长中的人自然会留在身后的东西。

intro.en: Outgrow is built from the Old English prefix out- and the verb grow, and it has spawned the noun outgrowth.
intro.cn: outgrow 由古英语前缀 out- 与动词 grow 组成，并派生出名词 outgrowth。

latinIntro.en: The parts are old English rather than Latin, but the verb grow is related through Germanic roots to Latin crescere.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的部件来自古英语而非拉丁语，不过动词 grow 通过日耳曼语词根与拉丁语 crescere 同源。

items.example: The prefix out- marks going beyond a limit.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 表示超出某个界限。

items.example: Grow is the Old English verb growan.
items.exampleCN: grow 源自古英语动词 growan。

items.example: The noun growth shares the same base.
items.exampleCN: 名词 growth 共享同一个基础词。

items.example: Outgrow keeps the sense of growing beyond.
items.exampleCN: outgrow 保留了「长得超出」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -th forms the noun outgrowth.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -th 构成名词 outgrowth。

items.example: The suffix -th turns grow into growth.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -th 把 grow 变成 growth。

items.example: The prefix over- forms overgrown.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 overgrown。

items.example: Outlast shares the prefix out- with outgrow.
items.exampleCN: outlast 与 outgrow 共享前缀 out-。

items.example: Outnumber also uses the surpassing sense of out-.
items.exampleCN: outnumber 也使用 out- 的「胜过」之意。

definition_zh: 逃犯；亡命之徒；宣布……为非法；取缔；使……失去法律保护
definition_en: a criminal who has escaped or is hiding from the law, or to declare that something is illegal and forbidden
core_image: 一个被赶出法律之外的人，独自站在城墙外的荒野里
scene: 中世纪的英格兰，犯下重罪又逃避审判的人会被宣布不受法律保护。A man declared an outlaw could be killed by anyone and had no right to courts or property.
sceneCN: 这里 outlaw 是「逃犯、被剥夺法律保护的人」（第 2 个义项：被宣布置于法律之外的人）；句意：一个被宣布为逃犯的人，任何人都可以杀死他，他没有上法庭的权利，也无权拥有财产。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转来的形容词，义为「被取缔的；非法的」
outlaw + -ry 构成的名词，法律术语，义为「（宣布为）不受法律保护；剥夺法律权利」

senses.title: A criminal who is on the run
senses.definition: a person who has broken the law and is living outside it, often hiding or on the run
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律并逃离法律管辖的人，常常在躲藏或逃亡
senses.example: The outlaw was finally caught at a river crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 那个逃犯最终在一个渡口被抓获。
senses.why: Because the word began as a legal label, even the plain sense keeps a hint of someone who stands outside the law.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个字原本是法律标签，所以即使最普通的义项也带着「站在法律之外」的影子。

senses.title: Someone stripped of legal protection
senses.titleCN: 被宣布不受法律保护的人
senses.definition: in medieval law, a person declared outside the protection of the law and denied all legal rights
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪法律中指被宣布置于法律的保护之外、一切法定权利被剥夺的人
senses.example: To be declared an outlaw meant losing the right to own land.
senses.exampleCN: 被宣布为亡命之徒，就意味着丧失拥有土地的权利。
senses.why: In Old English a man was placed outside the law by royal or local power, so the word codes a legal exile rather than a mere criminal.
senses.whyCN: 在古英语时期，一个人是被王权或地方权力「置于法律之外」的，所以这个词记录的是一种法律上的放逐，而不只是罪犯身份。

senses.title: To make something illegal
senses.definition: to make an activity or practice illegal by official order
senses.definitionCN: 通过官方命令使某种活动或做法成为非法
senses.example: Many countries have outlawed single-use plastic bags.
senses.exampleCN: 许多国家已经取缔了一次性塑料袋。
senses.why: The verb reverses the old wording: instead of putting a person outside the law, the law now puts a practice outside itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把旧说法倒了过来：以前是法律把一个人放到外面，现在是法律把一种做法放到自己之外。

senses.title: A figure in stories and films
senses.titleCN: （故事、电影中的）法外之徒形象
senses.definition: a romanticised figure in westerns, songs, and films who lives by his own code
senses.definitionCN: 西部片、民谣与电影中被浪漫化的形象，按自己的规矩行事
senses.example: In the western, the heroic outlaw robs the railroad company.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部西部片里，这位侠盗式的法外之徒抢劫了铁路公司。
senses.why: American frontier stories turned the hated legal status into a rebel hero who defies corrupt authority.
senses.whyCN: 美国边疆故事把这个人人畏惧的法律身份翻转成了反抗腐败权威的英雄，于是有了「侠盗」义项。

intro.en: Outlaw is a native English compound of out and the Old Norse word log, meaning law, formed in the late Old English period.
intro.cn: outlaw 是英语本族语复合词，由 out 与古诺斯语 log（法律）在古英语晚期构成。

items.en: Norwegians who settled in England brought log, meaning law.
items.cn: 迁居英格兰的挪威人带来了 log，意为「法律」。

items.en: Utlagu means one who has been put outside the law.
items.cn: 古英语 utlagu 指被置于法律之外的人。

items.en: French-speaking courts record the same idea with a parallel form.
items.cn: 讲法语的法庭用相近的形式记录同一概念。

items.en: Outlaw names both the legal status and the person who holds it.
items.cn: 中古英语 outlaw 既指这种法律身份，也指处于该身份的人。

items.en: The noun widens to hardened criminals and robbers in ballads.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，名词在民谣中扩展到惯犯与强盗。

items.en: A verb appears, meaning to make a practice illegal.
items.cn: 现代英语出现动词用法，表示使某种做法非法。

note.en: Outlaw belongs to the out- compound family and to a field of words about crime, prohibition, and the law.
note.cn: outlaw 属于 out- 复合词家族，同时也是犯罪、禁止与法律这一义场中的词。

entries.definition: a person rejected by a group or society
entries.definitionCN: 被群体或社会排斥的人

entries.definition: a strong feeling of anger at something unfair
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒；暴行。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a rare old word for a person outside a band or group
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的古词，指不属于某团体的人。只是与 outlaw 相近，构词来源不同

entries.definition: someone who is running away from the police
a robber who attacks travellers on the road
to forbid something officially

normalIntro.en: Outlaw simply means outside the law, and the word has kept that legal picture for a thousand years.
normalIntro.cn: outlaw 字面就是「在法律之外」，这个词把这幅法律画面保留了一千年。

normal.en: Break the word into out and law to see the criminal standing beyond the law.
normal.cn: 把词拆成 out 与 law，就能看到罪犯站在法律之外。

normal.en: The law part comes from Old Norse log, brought by settlers.
normal.cn: law 这一部分来自古诺斯语 log，由移民带来。

normal.en: Compare the legal pair inlaw and outlaw.
normal.cn: 对比法律上的成对概念 inlaw 与 outlaw。

normal.en: The verb has a passive look: an outlawed practice.
normal.cn: 动词常有被动色彩：an outlawed practice。

normal.en: Related out- compounds include outcast and outlandish.
normal.cn: 相关的 out- 复合词还有 outcast 与 outlandish。

abstract.en: See a barred gate with a man standing on the wrong side of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇上了门闩的大门，一个人站在门外的错误一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a wanted poster nailed to a tavern wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一张通缉令钉在酒馆的墙上。

abstract.en: Think of a red line drawn across a warning sign, meaning it is now banned.
abstract.cn: 想象告示牌上的标志被画了一道红线，表示从此被禁。

examples.en: The sheriff hunted the outlaw through three counties.
examples.cn: 治安官追捕那个逃犯，一路追踪了三个郡。

examples.en: In ancient times, an outlaw could be killed without trial.
examples.cn: 古代一个人若被判不受法律保护，可不经审判就被杀死。

examples.en: The government moved to outlaw smoking in public places.
examples.cn: 政府着手取缔在公共场所吸烟的行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特拉」——奥妙的特级大盗逃到栏杆（law）之外；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语 log（法律）与英语 out（在外）合成 → 古英语 utlagu（被置于法律之外者）→ 中古英语 outlaw：核心义「法律之外」，既是身份也是罪名。

sensesIntro.en: Outlaw runs from the legal status of a man placed outside the law to the everyday meaning of a criminal, then to the modern verb for banning a practice, and at last to the romantic figure of the stories.
sensesIntro.cn: outlaw 属于古英语法律术语，核心是「法律之外」：先是被剥夺法律保护的法定身份，再是日常所说的罪犯，然后转作动词表示「取缔」，最后成为故事中浪漫化的侠盗形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing beyond the boundary line of the law.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在法律的边界线之外。

branches.en: The everyday criminal sense grew from the legal label.
branches.cn: 日常所说「罪犯」的意思是从法律标签长出来的。

branches.en: The strict legal meaning is exile from the protection of the law.
branches.cn: 最严格的法律义是被剥夺法律保护。

branches.en: The verb bans a practice instead of a person, reversing the direction.
branches.cn: 动词取缔的是做法而不是人，方向正好倒过来。

branches.en: Story and film turn the outlaw into a hero who defies corrupt power.
branches.cn: 故事与电影把法外之徒塑造成反抗腐败权力的英雄。

branches.en: Both the criminal and the legal exile live at the edge of society.
branches.cn: 罪犯与法律上的放逐者都生活于社会的边缘。

intro.en: Outlaw combines the English prefix out- with law, a word borrowed from Old Norse, and has given rise to noun, adjective, and verb forms.
intro.cn: outlaw 把英语前缀 out- 与借自古诺斯语的 law 组合在一起，并衍生出名词、形容词和动词形式。

latinIntro.en: The parts of the word come from Old English and Old Norse rather than Latin, so no Latin same-root words are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的部件来自古英语与古诺斯语，而非拉丁语，因此不另列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The prefix out- places the person outside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 把人放到某个界限之外。

items.example: Law comes from Old Norse log.
items.exampleCN: law 来自古诺斯语 log。

items.example: Outlaw began as a legal status.
items.exampleCN: outlaw 最初是一种法律身份。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms outlawed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 outlawed。

items.meaning: the state of being outside the law
items.example: The suffix -ry forms the legal noun outlawry.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ry 构成法律名词 outlawry。

items.example: Outcast shares the prefix out-.
items.exampleCN: outcast 共享前缀 out-。

items.example: Outlandish also builds on the idea of outside.
items.exampleCN: outlandish 同样建立在「在外」的观念上。

items.meaning: to restore a person to the protection of the law
items.example: Inlaw is the legal opposite of outlaw.
items.exampleCN: inlaw 是 outlaw 的法律反义用法。

definition_zh: 异常值；离群数据；局外人；远离主体的事物；孤立者
definition_en: a value, place, or person that lies far away from the main group or pattern
core_image: 一排整齐的点里，有一个点孤零零地漂在外面很远的地方
scene: 统计课上，老师把全班同学的身高标在一张散点图上。Most of the dots crowded round the average, but one dot sat far above the rest as a clear outlier.
sceneCN: 这里 outlier 是「异常值、离群数据」（第 1 个义项：统计中远离主体的数值）；句意：大多数点都挤在平均值附近，但有一个点高高地飘在上面，明显是个异常值。

pos.zh: 异常值；离群值；局外人；孤立的人或物

collocations.zh: 地理位置上的边缘分布点

derivatives.zh: out + lying 构成，义为「偏远的外围的」，由「躺在外面」这一意象转来，与 outlier 同源
out + lie 构成的动词，义为「位于……更远处；在外围」，罕见的同源词

senses.title: A value far from the rest
senses.definition: a data point that lies far outside the general pattern of a set of values
senses.definitionCN: 远远偏离一组数值总体规律的数据点
senses.example: One outlier pulled the average salary far above the median.
senses.exampleCN: 一个异常值把平均工资拉得远高于中位数。
senses.why: The word takes its picture from statistics: a single number that lies out, outside the cloud of the others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的意象取自统计：单个数字「躺在外面」，落在其他数值组成的一团之外，所以叫异常值。

senses.title: A person outside the group
senses.definition: a person who differs from or is not accepted by the rest of a group
senses.definitionCN: 与群体中其余人不同或不被群体接受的人
senses.example: As a quiet child, he was something of an outlier at school.
senses.exampleCN: 他从小安静，在学校里多少算个局外人。
senses.why: The statistical picture of a dot standing apart is easily carried over to a person standing apart from the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 「一个点孤立在外面」的统计画面很容易迁移到人身上：一个人与人群保持距离，就成了局外人。

senses.title: A place away from the main area
senses.titleCN: 远离主体的地方；孤立区域
senses.definition: a small area or settlement lying far from the main body of a region
senses.definitionCN: 远离某一地区主体部分的小块区域或聚居地
senses.example: The island is a remote outlier of the main archipelago.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛是主群岛中一个偏远的孤立岛屿。
senses.why: Place names use the word in its literal lying-out sense, for ground that sits apart from the main block.
senses.whyCN: 地名中用的是字面的「躺在外面」，指一块土地与主体分离，于是有了「孤立区域」义。

senses.title: A result unlike the others
senses.titleCN: 与众不同的结果；例外情况
senses.definition: a result or performance in sport, business, or research that departs sharply from the usual run
senses.definitionCN: 体育、商业或研究中明显偏离通常水平的结果或表现
senses.example: Their record sales last year were an outlier in a weak market.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年的破纪录销量在低迷的市场中是个例外。
senses.why: Once the word names a data point that does not fit, it can label any event that fails to follow the expected pattern.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指代「不符合规律的数据点」，它就可以用来标记任何没有遵循预期套路的事件。

intro.en: Outlier is an English compound of out and the verb lie, formed in the sixteenth century to describe land lying apart from the main area.
intro.cn: outlier 是英语复合词，由 out 与动词 lie 构成，十六世纪出现，最初描述与主体分开的一块土地。

items.en: The pieces out and licgan already described where something lies.
items.cn: 古英语中 out 与 licgan 已可描述某物所处的位置。

items.en: Outlier first names an outlier of rock, a piece of land detached from a larger formation.
items.cn: 十六世纪 outlier 最初指远离主体岩层的孤立岩块。

items.en: It extends to remote farms and settlements outside a main area.
items.cn: 十七世纪扩展到主体区域之外的偏远农舍与聚居地。

items.en: Statistics takes up the word for a value lying far from the rest.
items.cn: 十九世纪统计学采用这个词，指远离其余数值的值。

items.en: Business and sport writing use outlier for any exceptional result or person.
items.cn: 二十世纪商业与体育写作把 outlier 用于任何例外结果或例外人物。

note.en: Outlier is close in spelling to outliner and consists of the parts out and lie, while its meaning sits near terms for exceptions and deviant cases.
note.cn: outlier 与 outliner 拼写相近，构词部件是 out 与 lie；在意思上它靠近「例外、偏离者」这一类词。

entries.definition: a tool or person that makes outlines
entries.definitionCN: 画轮廓的工具或人。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a line that marks the edge of a shape
entries.definitionCN: 轮廓；大纲。只是拼写相近，构词不同

entries.definition: far from the centre of an area
a case that does not follow a general rule
something that differs from an expected pattern
a person whose behaviour differs from the norm

normalIntro.en: Outlier is simply something that lies out, apart from the crowd, and that picture explains every sense.
normalIntro.cn: outlier 就是「躺在外面」的东西，与人群分开，这幅画面能解释它的所有义项。

normal.en: Split the word into out and lier to see a thing lying outside the group.
normal.cn: 把词拆成 out 与 lier，就能看到一样东西躺在群外。

normal.en: The -er ending marks the person or thing that does the lying out.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 表示「处于……状态的人或物」。

normal.en: Compare outlying, the adjective for scattered settlements far from a centre.
normal.cn: 对比形容词 outlying，指远离中心的分散聚落。

normal.en: In statistics an outlier is a value far from the median or the mean.
normal.cn: 统计学里 outlier 是远离中位数或平均数的值。

normal.en: Keep the rhythm: out plus lieer, stress on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 记住重音：outlier 的重音落在第一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a flock of birds flying together and one bird far off to the side.
abstract.cn: 想象一群鸟一起飞，有一只鸟远远地飞在侧边。

abstract.en: See a classroom seating chart with one desk alone by the window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张教室座位表，只有一张桌子单独靠着窗。

abstract.en: Picture a large island with one small island alone on the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一座大岛，天边另有一座孤零零的小岛。

examples.en: The researchers left out three outliers before plotting the trend.
examples.cn: 研究人员在绘制趋势线之前剔除了三个异常值。

examples.en: He was an outlier among his classmates, preferring books to games.
examples.cn: 在同学中间他是个局外人，更喜欢书而不是游戏。

examples.en: One unusually wet month was an outlier in the record.
examples.cn: 记录中有一个异常多雨的月份，是一个例外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特莱尔」——奥特曼单独躺（lier）在外围，孤零零一个；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 out（在外）+ 动词 lie（躺、位于）→ out + lier → outlier：核心义「躺在外面」，指与主体分离的岩块、区域或数值。

sensesIntro.en: Outlier began with rock and land lying outside a main formation, then entered statistics as a value outside the pattern, and spread to people and results that stand apart from the group.
sensesIntro.cn: outlier 最初指躺在主体地层之外的岩块与土地，后来进入统计学指偏离规律的数据，再扩展到与群体不同的人以及异乎寻常的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one dot standing well outside the line of its neighbours.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点离邻近的一排点远远地站着。

branches.en: Statistics names a number that lies outside the pattern.
branches.cn: 统计学把偏离规律的数字命名为异常值。

branches.en: A person apart from the group borrows the same spatial picture.
branches.cn: 与群体分开的人借用了同样的空间画面。

branches.en: Geographers use it literally for land detached from the main area.
branches.cn: 地理学中最字面地指与主体区域分离的土地。

branches.en: Market and sport results that break the usual line are outliers too.
branches.cn: 打破通常曲线的市场与体育成绩也属于例外。

branches.en: Both a data point and a record result stand away from what is expected.
branches.cn: 数据点与破纪录成绩都偏离了预期。

intro.en: Outlier is formed from the English prefix out- and the verb lie, with the agent ending -er, and it has close relatives in outlying and outlie.
intro.cn: outlier 由英语前缀 out- 与动词 lie 组成，并带表「人或物」的 -er 词尾，与 outlying、outlie 是近亲。

latinIntro.en: The parts of the word are English or Old English, not Latin, so there are no Latin same-root words to list.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的部件来自英语与古英语，而非拉丁语，因此没有需要单列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: The prefix out- points to something outside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 指向在外面的事物。

items.example: Lie here means to be situated.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 lie 意为「位于」。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.example: The suffix -er forms the agent noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成表示「人或物」的名词。

items.example: Outlier is the noun of lying outside.
items.exampleCN: outlier 是「位于外面」的名词形式。

items.example: The ending -ing forms the adjective outlying.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成形容词 outlying。

items.example: Outlie is the verb behind outlier.
items.exampleCN: outlie 是 outlier 背后的动词。

items.example: Outline shares out- but not the word lie.
items.exampleCN: outline 共享 out-，但不含 lie。

items.example: Outlaw also builds with out-.
items.exampleCN: outlaw 也用 out- 构成。

items.example: Outsider is the nearest out- noun in meaning.
items.exampleCN: 在意义上最接近的 out- 名词是 outsider。

definition_zh: 超过……的速度；比……发展得快；（在竞争中）胜过、甩开
definition_en: to go faster than someone or something else, or to grow or develop more quickly than they do
core_image: 两条并排的跑道：外侧那条腿越迈越快，渐渐把隔壁跑道甩在身后
scene: 马拉松跑到一半，两名领跑者仍并排前进。In the last mile the young runner outpaced his rival.
sceneCN: 这里 outpace 是「超过……的速度」（第 1 个义项：跑得比对手或同伴更快）；句意：最后一英里，这位年轻跑者超过了对手。画面中可辨识物件：跑道、计时钟、号码布。

pos.zh: 动词：跑得比……快；速度或发展超过；在竞争中胜过

derivatives.zh: 借过去分词转作形容词，义为「被超越的；落在后面的」，多用于 be outpaced 结构
现在分词转作名词，义为「超越；领先于他人的速度或增长」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「跑得更快者；增长更快的竞争者」，多见于商业评论

senses.title: To run or ride faster than a rival
senses.titleCN: 跑得比对手快；在竞速中超过
senses.definition: to move faster than another runner, rider, or vehicle so that you get ahead of them
senses.definitionCN: 比对手（跑者、骑手或车辆）移动得更快，从而跑到前面去
senses.example: On the final climb she outpaced the other cyclists.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一段爬坡中，她把其他车手甩在了后面。
senses.why: Pace first means the rate of walking or running, and out- says to go beyond, so to outpace is literally to run beyond another pace.
senses.whyCN: pace 本义是走或跑的快慢，out- 表示「超出」，所以 outpace 字面上就是「把别人甩在身后的一段速度」，义项直接来自这两部分。

senses.title: To grow or change faster than something else
senses.definition: to increase at a faster rate than another measure, group, or system
senses.definitionCN: 增长速度超过另一项指标、群体或体系
senses.example: House prices have outpaced wages for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 十年来房价的涨速一直快于工资。
senses.why: When the race is about numbers rather than legs, pace shifts to the speed of growth, so outpacing becomes an economic comparison of two curves.
senses.whyCN: 当比赛的对象从腿脚换成数字时，pace 就从「跑速」变成了「增速」，outpacing 于是成为两条曲线的经济比较。

senses.title: To leave a competitor behind in a contest
senses.definition: to be of better quality or more successful than another person or company
senses.definitionCN: 在质量或业绩上比对手更好、更成功
senses.example: The smaller firm has outpaced bigger rivals in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小公司在销售上超过了规模更大的对手。
senses.why: Ahead of the others in a race also means ahead in status, so the verb carries over to markets where no one is actually running.
senses.whyCN: 比赛里跑在别人前面，也意味着地位领先；于是这个词被搬到市场上，尽管那里并没有人真的在跑。

senses.title: To go beyond what the world can handle
senses.definition: to rise beyond what a society, system, or supply can afford or absorb
senses.definitionCN: 上升到社会、制度或供给无法负担或承受的水平
senses.example: The growth in the number of cars has outpaced the road network.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车数量的增长已经超过了道路网的承载能力。
senses.why: If one thing moves faster than another can follow, the follower falls behind, so outpacing can describe demand running away from supply.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个东西动得比另一个快、后者跟不上，后者就被落在后面；所以 outpacing 也可以描述需求甩开供给的情形。

intro.en: Outpace is a transparent English compound of out- and pace, made in the early modern period, and it does not descend from Latin pace.
intro.cn: outpace 是 out- 与 pace 组合而成的英语复合词，产生于近代早期，与拉丁语词根 pax 无关。

items.en: The noun pace goes back to Latin passus, a step or stride, from pandere, to spread out. This is the historical root of pace the noun, not of the Latin word pax meaning peace.
items.cn: 名词 pace 上溯拉丁语 passus（一步、跨步），出自 pandere（展开）。这是 pace 作名词的历史词根，而不是拉丁语 pax（和平）。

items.en: Through Old French pas or pace the word reached Middle English as pace, meaning a step or the length of a step.
items.cn: 经由古法语 pas 或 pace，这个词进入中古英语作 pace，意为「一步」或「步长」。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the noun pace also meant speed or rate of movement, a sense recorded in the period when English compounds with out- were multiplying.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，名词 pace 又指「速度、移动的快慢」，这一义项出现的时期正是英语中 out- 复合词大量增多的年代。

items.en: The verb outpace is generally dated to the eighteenth century, formed on the pattern of outrun and outstrip. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 outpace 一般认为形成于十八世纪，仿照 outrun、outstrip 的模式构成；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Business and economics writing has pushed outpace beyond running: prices, wages, demand and sales now outpace one another.
items.cn: 商业与经济写作把 outpace 带出了跑道：如今物价、工资、需求与销量都可以互相「跑赢」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the out- compounds and the related pace and pass words; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of overtaking and outrunning with different degrees of speed.
note.cn: 形近组收 out- 复合词以及与 pace、pass 相关的词；近义组收「超过、赶超」一类动词，速度快慢各有侧重。

entries.definition: The rate or speed at which someone walks, runs, or something develops; the word outpace is built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「步速、速度、节奏」，是 outpace 的基础词，其拉丁词根是 passus（一步）。

entries.definition: To run faster than someone, or to escape something by going faster, sharing the same out- pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「跑得比……快、甩开」，与 outpace 同属 out- 复合词，仅对象是「跑」的动作。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a step or stride, the source of pace and of the pas- family; not related to pax, meaning peace.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语名词，意为「一步、跨步」，是 pace 以及 pas- 词族的来源，与表示和平的 pax 无关。

entries.definition: To come from behind and pass someone; it stresses position rather than the speed of growth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赶上并超过」，从后面追上来并越过，强调位置变化而非增长快慢。

entries.definition: To do better than another or increase faster; very close to outpace in business writing.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「超过、胜过」，在商业语境中与 outpace 非常接近，常与 demand 或 supply 连用。

entries.definition: To be better or greater than something; more about quality and quantity than about speed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「胜过、超越」，语气正式，侧重质量或数量而非速度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts of the compound, its running origin, and the phrases it now appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子利用这个复合词的真实构词成分、它与赛跑的渊源，以及如今的常见搭配。

normal.en: Out plus pace: to go beyond the other persons pace.
normal.cn: out（超出）加 pace（步伐、速度）：超出别人的步伐，就是跑赢。

normal.en: Pace comes from Latin passus, a step, so outpacing means taking steps faster and further.
normal.cn: pace 源自拉丁语 passus（一步），所以 outpacing 就是步子迈得更快、更远。

normal.en: In news headlines, prices or rent often outpace wages.
normal.cn: 在新闻标题里，物价或房租常常 outpace 工资，表示涨得比工资快。

normal.en: Outrun, outstrip, outnumber and outlive share the same out- pattern of beating someone in some respect.
normal.cn: outrun、outstrip、outnumber、outlive 都采用同一 out- 构词式，表示在某方面胜过对方。

normal.en: Be outpaced by a rival means the rival has overtaken you.
normal.cn: be outpaced by a rival 意为被对手赶超、落在后面。

abstract.en: Picture two lanes of a running track and one pair of shoes moving a little quicker each lap.
abstract.cn: 想象两条并排的跑道，其中一个选手每圈都快一点，最后慢慢拉开了距离。

abstract.en: See two lines on a chart, one racing upward while the other crawls.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图表上的两条曲线，一条飞快上扬，另一条慢慢爬行。

abstract.en: Think of a fast train leaving a slow cart behind on the same rails.
abstract.cn: 想象同一轨道上一列快车把慢车远远甩在后面。

examples.en: Technology often outpaces the rules that are meant to control it.
examples.cn: 技术发展常常快于旨在约束它的法规。

examples.en: Few runners in that race could keep up, and none could outpace her.
examples.cn: 那场比赛中很少有人跟得上，也没人跑得过她。

examples.en: Demand for these seats has outpaced supply for the whole year.
examples.cn: 这类座位的需求量整年都超过了供给。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特佩斯」——奥特曼速度超快，把配速甩在身后；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 out-（超出、在外）+ pace（步速），构成动词「跑得比……快」。pace 作名词时源自拉丁语 passus（一步），出自 pandere（展开）；它与拉丁语 pax「和平」及短语 pace「请……谅解」没有词源关系。outpace 一般认为形成于十八世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Outpace moves from a foot race to growth rates to markets and finally to anything that rises faster than a system can absorb.
sensesIntro.cn: outpace 从跑步竞速出发，先用于数字与增长率，再用于市场竞争，最后泛指任何涨得比承受能力更快的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two runners on parallel lanes, and one pulls gradually ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排跑道上，其中一人渐渐跑到前面。

branches.en: THE BODY: faster legs win the race, the most literal sense.
branches.cn: 身体层面：腿脚更快的一方赢得比赛，是最字面的义项。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: two growth rates are compared, and one curve climbs faster.
branches.cn: 数字层面：比较两个增长率，其中一条曲线爬升得更快。

branches.en: THE MARKET: being ahead in sales means outrunning the rivals.
branches.cn: 市场层面：销量领先就等于跑赢了对手。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: when demand outpaces supply, speed turns into a burden.
branches.cn: 限度层面：需求超过供给时，速度反而变成了负担。

branches.en: Both the fastest runner and runaway demand leave the others behind.
branches.cn: 跑得最快的选手与失控的需求，都把其余的甩在了后面。

intro.en: Outpace is a modern out- compound; English bits build the word, and the base noun pace carries the Latin root passus.
intro.cn: outpace 是近代的 out- 复合词，由英语构件组合而成，基础名词 pace 则携带拉丁词根 passus。

latinIntro.en: The out- prefix is native English, not Latin; only pace has a Latin source, the noun passus from pandere.
latinIntro.cn: out- 是英语本族前缀，并非拉丁语；只有 pace 有拉丁来源，即出自 pandere 的名词 passus。

items.example: The prefix out- turns pace into outpacing a rival.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 让 pace 变成「胜过对手」。

items.example: Pace supplies the measure that is beaten.
items.exampleCN: pace 提供被超越的那个「速度」。

items.example: Passus lies behind pace as a unit of walking.
items.exampleCN: passus 是 pace 作为「一步」单位的来源。

items.example: The suffix -ed gives outpaced.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 outpaced。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives outpacing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 outpacing。

items.example: The suffix -s gives outpaces.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 outpaces。

items.example: Outrun is the model that outpace follows.
items.exampleCN: outrun 是 outpace 仿照的模型词。

items.example: Outstrip is a near synonym built the same way.
items.exampleCN: outstrip 是用同样方式构成的近义词。

items.example: The runner was outpaced in the final lap.
items.exampleCN: 那位跑者在最后一圈被超越。

definition_zh: 前哨；边哨；偏远驻地；（商业或地区的）前哨据点、分支机构
definition_en: a small military camp or settlement far from the main force, or a distant office or base used to open up a new area
core_image: 荒野尽头立着几根木桩和一面旗帜，城墙与主力部队都远在身后
scene: 地图上代表城市的那一点已经小了，四周尽是灰绿色的荒野。A few soldiers kept watch at the lone outpost at the edge of the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 outpost 是「前哨」（第 1 个义项：远离主力的小型军事据点）；句意：几名士兵在山谷边缘那座孤零零的前哨里守望。画面中可辨识物件：木桩、哨旗、荒野。

pos.zh: 名词：（军事）前哨、边哨；偏远驻地；商业或探索的前哨据点

derivatives.zh: 由 outpost 加 -ed 转作形容词，义为「被派驻边远哨所的」，多见于军事与商务文体
由 outpost 加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「（机构）设立边远分支」，与派驻相关的现代构词

senses.title: A small military camp far from the main army
senses.definition: a small group of soldiers and their camp placed far from the main force to watch a border or a route
senses.definitionCN: 远离主力的少量士兵及其营地，负责监视边境或通道
senses.example: A handful of troops held the outpost through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 一队士兵在寒冬里守住了那座前哨。
senses.why: Post here means a position where soldiers are stationed, and out- marks it as standing outside the main body, so the camp becomes a forward point.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 post 指士兵驻守的位置，out- 表明它「在主阵地之外」，营地因此成了一个伸向前方的点。

senses.title: A distant settlement in a wild area
senses.definition: a small settlement or station that sits far from towns, often the first mark of people in a wild region
senses.definitionCN: 远离城镇的小聚落或站点，常是荒远地区里最早的居民痕迹
senses.example: That fishing village is the last outpost on the coast road.
senses.exampleCN: 那个渔村是沿海公路上最后的驻地。
senses.why: If a camp can stand far from the army, any small community can stand far from civilization, so the word opens up from soldiers to settlements.
senses.whyCN: 如果哨所可以远离军队，那么任何小社区也可以远离文明中心；于是这个词从士兵扩展到居民点。

senses.title: A branch used to open a new market
senses.titleCN: （商业或对外扩张的）前哨据点
senses.definition: a shop, office, or factory opened far from headquarters to test or open up a new region
senses.definitionCN: 远离总部开设的商店、办事处或工厂，用来试探或开拓一个新地区
senses.example: The bank opened its first overseas outpost in 1890.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行于一八九年在海外开设了第一个据点。
senses.why: Modern companies advance into new markets the way armies advance into new land, so a first office is named like a frontier camp.
senses.whyCN: 现代公司进入新市场，正如军队推进到新土地，于是开出的第一个办事处被称作前哨。

senses.title: A last remaining example of something
senses.definition: the last place where a practice, a species, or an idea still survives
senses.definitionCN: 某种做法、物种或观念最后还在延续的地方
senses.example: This valley is one of the last outposts of the old dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷是老方言最后的据点之一。
senses.why: The frontier image twists here: what is defended is no longer territory but a way of life that is losing ground.
senses.whyCN: 这里边界的意象发生了反转：所要守卫的不再是领土，而是一种正在退守的生活方式。

intro.en: Outpost joins English out and post, a place where someone is stationed, and it is not connected with Latin post meaning after.
intro.cn: outpost 由英语的 out 与 post（驻扎之地）组合而成，与表示「之后」的拉丁语 post 无关。

items.en: Latin positus, a placing, from ponere, to put, gives Italian posto and French poste, a place or station.
items.cn: 拉丁语 positus（放置，出自 ponere「放」）给出意大利语 posto 与法语 poste，意为「处所、岗位」。

items.en: By the sixteenth century English post meant the place where a soldier or sentinel took up duty: at his post.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，英语 post 已指士兵或哨兵上岗驻守的地方，如 at his post（在岗位上）。

items.en: Outpost is recorded in the eighteenth century in military writing as a detachment stationed beyond the main body. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: outpost 于十八世纪见于军事文字，指驻扎在主阵地之外的分遣队；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word spread from the army to pioneers, explorers and traders, who called their remote settlements outposts.
items.cn: 这个词从军队扩展到拓荒者、探险者与商人，这些人把自己偏远的聚落也称作 outpost。

items.en: Banks, airlines and research stations now call a first office in a new region an outpost.
items.cn: 如今银行、航空公司与研究站也把在新地区开设的第一个办事处称为 outpost。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other out- compounds and the post words; the near-meaning group gathers frontier, base and settlement terms with different military flavour.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 out- 复合词与 post 系列词；近义组收边境、基地与聚落一类词，军事色彩浓淡不同。

entries.definition: A place where someone is stationed or sent to work; the second half of outpost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「岗位、驻地、邮寄」，是 outpost 的后半部分，与拉丁语「之后」的 post 无关。

entries.definition: A view or a forecast; another English compound built with the same out- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观点、前景」，与 outpost 共用 out- 前缀，只是后半部分为 look。

entries.definition: The beginning of something; it shares the out- pattern but has no military sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「开始、开端」，与 outpost 同属 out- 复合词，却没有军事含义。

entries.definition: Troops stationed to defend a town or fortress; larger and more permanent than an outpost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「驻军、卫戍部队」或动词「驻守」，规模更大、更长期，通常驻守城镇或要塞。

entries.definition: A strong building or group of buildings made to resist attack; it stresses defence rather than distance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堡垒、要塞」，强调防御工事本身，而不强调离主力有多远。

entries.definition: The line or area where settlement meets wild land; the zone an outpost watches over.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「边境、边疆」，指居民区与荒野相接的地带，正是前哨守望的那片区域。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two halves of the compound and the way the word moved from army posts to business branches.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子利用这个复合词的两个成分，以及它从军事岗哨转向商业分支的历程。

normal.en: Out plus post: a post set outside the main camp.
normal.cn: out（在外）加 post（岗位）：设在主营地之外的岗位，就是前哨。

normal.en: Post comes through Italian posto from Latin positus, a placing, so an outpost is a place put outside.
normal.cn: post 经由意大利语 posto 来自拉丁语 positus（放置），所以 outpost 就是「被放在外面的一处地方」。

normal.en: Do not confuse this post with Latin post meaning after, as in post-war.
normal.cn: 不要把这里的 post 与表示「之后」的拉丁语 post 混为一谈，后者见于 post-war。

normal.en: A trading outpost was a remote base for goods and still carries the idea of a remote station.
normal.cn: trading outpost 是设在远方的货物据点，仍保留「远地站点」的含义。

normal.en: The last outpost of a custom means the only place it still survives.
normal.cn: 若说某风俗只剩一处据点，意思是它只在这个地方还留存着。

abstract.en: Picture a single tent with a flag on a plain, and the army tiny on the horizon behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象平原上一顶孤零零的帐篷和一面旗，身后的地平线上军队小得几乎看不见。

abstract.en: See a line of lights thinning out until one last lamp stands alone in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一排灯光越来越稀疏，最后只剩最后一盏孤灯留在黑暗里。

abstract.en: Think of a shop sign in a far city: a company sending one small branch ahead like a scout.
abstract.cn: 想象远城的一家店招牌：公司像派侦察兵一样，先派去一个小小的分支。

examples.en: The patrol returned to its outpost before dawn.
examples.cn: 巡逻队在黎明前回到了前哨。

examples.en: The company treats this small store as an outpost in a new market.
examples.cn: 公司把这间小店当作进入新市场的前哨。

examples.en: Only two families still live in that mountain outpost.
examples.cn: 那座山中据点如今只剩两户人家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特破司特」——奥特战士在破旧的哨亭外站岗：前哨。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 out（在外）+ post（岗位、驻地）构成的复合词。post 这个义项经意大利语 posto 来自拉丁语 positus（放置，出自 ponere「放」），与表示「之后」的拉丁语 post 无关。outpost 于十八世纪见于军事著作，后扩展到贸易据点与海外分支。

sensesIntro.en: Outpost starts as a military camp beyond the main force, widens to remote settlements, then to first branches abroad and finally to any last place where something survives.
sensesIntro.cn: outpost 起初指主力之外的军营，接着扩展到偏远聚落，再到海外第一间分支，最后泛指某种事物最后的留存之地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few posts and a flag standing alone far ahead of the main camp.
core.cn: 核心意象：几根木桩和一面旗孤零零地立在主营地很远的前方。

branches.en: THE ARMY: a forward post watches the border, the original sense.
branches.cn: 军事层面：前哨盯守边境，是最原始的义项。

branches.en: THE SETTLEMENT: people, not only soldiers, carry the camp into the wild.
branches.cn: 聚落层面：驻守的不再只是士兵，居民也把营地带入荒野。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a first overseas branch works like a frontier camp.
branches.cn: 市场层面：第一个海外分支机构如同边地营地。

branches.en: THE LAST HOLD: what is defended is a fading practice, not land.
branches.cn: 最后据点：被守卫的不再是土地，而是一种将逝的做法。

branches.en: Both the soldier post and the remote village stand far from the centre.
branches.cn: 军事岗哨与偏远村落都远离中心，这正是两者共通之处。

intro.en: Outpost is an English compound: a native out- prefix plus post, whose place meaning traces back to Latin positus.
intro.cn: outpost 是英语复合词：本族前缀 out- 加 post，而 post 的「处所」义可上溯拉丁语 positus。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere, to put, and its participle positus, a placing, underlie post, position and posit as well as the place sense of post.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ponere（放）及其分词 positus（放置）是 post、position、posit 等的来源，也包括 post 的「处所」义。

items.example: The prefix out- places the post beyond the main body.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 out- 把岗位放到主阵地之外。

items.meaning: a place where one is stationed
items.example: Post supplies the station that the compound names.
items.exampleCN: post 提供这个复合词所指的「驻地」。

items.example: Ponere is the deeper source of the place sense.
items.exampleCN: ponere 是「处所」义的更深来源。

items.example: The suffix -s gives outposts.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 outposts。

items.example: Outposted guards served far from base.
items.exampleCN: 被派出的守卫远离基地执勤。

items.example: Outlook shares the out- pattern of outpost.
items.exampleCN: outlook 与 outpost 共用 out- 构词式。

items.example: Outset is a close look-alike in spelling.
items.exampleCN: outset 在拼写上与本词很接近。

items.example: Outstanding is built with the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: outstanding 用同一前缀构成。

items.example: A garrison holds a town while an outpost holds a point.
items.exampleCN: 驻军守住城镇，前哨守住一个点。

definition_zh: 暴行；骇人的恶行；愤慨、义愤；使人愤怒的事；激怒
definition_en: a cruel or shocking act, the strong anger it causes, or a thing seen as deeply unfair, and the verb meaning to shock and anger someone
core_image: 天平被重物狠狠砸歪，旁边围观的众人握紧拳头、脸色涨红
scene: 老桥被拆的消息一贴出来，乡里人就围在公告栏前议论不休。News of the closure caused outrage among the villagers.
sceneCN: 这里 outrage 是「愤慨、义愤」（第 3 个义项：因不公或恶行而生的强烈愤怒）；句意：关闭桥梁的消息令村民们非常愤怒。画面中可辨识物件：公告栏、握紧的拳头、皱起的眉。

pos.zh: 名词：暴行、骇人的恶行；愤慨、义愤；使人愤怒的事

derivatives.zh: 借过去分词转作形容词，义为「愤慨的；被激怒的」，如 outraged residents
由本词加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「骇人的；离谱的；令人愤慨的」
由 outrageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「离谱地；令人震惊地」
由 outrageous 加 -ness 构成，义为「骇人听闻；离谱的程度」

senses.title: A cruel or shocking act
senses.definition: a violent, cruel, or deeply shocking act that goes far beyond what is acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 极端残忍或骇人听闻的行径，远远超出可接受的范围
senses.example: The burning of the village was remembered as an outrage.
senses.exampleCN: 焚毁村庄的那一幕被当作一场暴行记了下来。
senses.why: The word comes through French from Latin ultra, beyond, so an outrage is first an act that goes beyond every limit of right and decency.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语 ultra（超出），所以 outrage 首先是一种越过了正当与体面界限的行为。

senses.title: A deeply unfair treatment
senses.titleCN: 不公之事；令人愤慨的事
senses.definition: a deed or official act that is seen as grossly unfair or insulting
senses.definitionCN: 被视为极不公平或带侮辱性的行为或官方举措
senses.example: Ten years in prison for such a minor offence is an outrage.
senses.exampleCN: 为这么小的过错判十年监禁，实在令人愤慨。
senses.why: The same beyond-limit image applies to rules and rulings: when punishment or treatment overshoots what is fair, the act is named outrage.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「越界」的意象也适用于规则与判决：当惩罚或待遇大大超出公平限度时，这件事就被叫作 outrage。

senses.title: Strong anger at something wrong
senses.definition: a strong feeling of anger and shock caused by something that seems inhuman or unfair
senses.definitionCN: 由似乎不人道或不公平的事引起的强烈愤怒与震惊
senses.example: There was widespread outrage at the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 这项决定引发了广泛的愤慨。
senses.why: Because the act first shocks people, outrage came to name the response as well: the blow is outside the limit, and the feeling rises to match it.
senses.whyCN: 因为越界之举首先震惊了众人，outrage 便也用来指这种反应：打击越出常理，愤怒也随之高涨到同样的高度。

senses.title: To shock and anger someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel extremely angry and morally shocked
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到极度愤怒并受到道德上的冲击
senses.example: The fee hike outraged passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 涨价让乘客们大为愤慨。
senses.why: Once the noun meant both the act and the feeling, English turned it into a verb meaning to cause that feeling in someone.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已兼指行为与感受之后，英语又把它转为动词，表示「使某人产生那种愤慨」。

intro.en: Outrage comes through French from Latin ultra, beyond, with the French letter u later heard as English o; it has nothing to do with rage.
intro.cn: outrage 经法语来自拉丁语 ultra（超出），法语的 u 后来在英语中读成了 o；它与英语 rage 也就是「狂怒」并无词源关系。

items.en: Latin ultra means beyond, on the far side, and is the ancestor of the prefix ultra- in ultra-modern and ultrasonic.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ultra 意为「超出、在更远处」，也是 ultra-modern、ultrasonic 中前缀 ultra- 的祖先。

items.en: Old French outrage or oltrage mean excess or violence, built on the stem ult- with the -age noun suffix.
items.cn: 古法语 outrage 或 oltrage 意为「过分、暴行」，由词干 ult- 加名词后缀 -age 构成。

items.en: Middle English took outrage as an act of excess or violence. The first spelling and date are uncertain; the initial o reflects French pronunciation.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 outrage 表示「过分之举、暴行」；首见拼写与年代不确定，开头的 o 反映法语的读音。

items.en: The modern sense of a cruel or shocking act is joined by the sense of strong anger in this period; the senses overlap because one causes the other.
items.cn: 「骇人恶行」的现代义在这一时期与「强烈愤怒」的义项并存；两者彼此交叠，前者正是后者的起因。

items.en: The verb outrage, to shock and anger, spreads in journalism, using outrage as a newspaper word for public fury.
items.cn: 动词 outrage（使愤慨）在新闻文体中广为流行，outrage 也成了报纸表达「公愤」的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the ult- family and the misleading rage word; the near-meaning group gathers anger and misconduct nouns with different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收 ult- 词族与容易误导的 rage；近义组收表示「愤怒」与「恶行」的名词，强度各不相同。

entries.definition: Extreme violent anger; it ends like outrage and means anger, but outrage is not built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「狂怒」；与 outrage 词尾相同、含义相近，但 outrage 并非由它构成，属于拼写相似而词源不同。

entries.definition: Extremely angry and shocked, formed directly from outrage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「愤慨的、被激怒的」，由本词直接加 -d 构成。

entries.definition: Extremely shocking, unfair, or wild, formed with the suffix -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「骇人的、离谱的」，由本词加后缀 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning extremely or beyond; the Latin source of the first part of outrage.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀，义为「极端、超出」，其拉丁语 ultra 正是 outrage 前半部分的来源。

entries.definition: Anger caused by something unfair or unworthy; calmer and more formal than outrage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「义愤、愤慨」，由不公或可耻之事引起，语气比 outrage 更平静、更正式。

entries.definition: Very great and often uncontrolled anger; it stresses heat without the moral judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「狂怒」，强度极大且常失控，强调情绪之火，不含道德评判。

entries.definition: A very cruel act, especially against civilians; it is the act itself, without the anger sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴行」，尤指针对平民的极残忍行为，只指行为本身，不含愤怒义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use out, the Latin ultra behind it, and the words that grow from outrage in modern English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子利用 out、其背后的拉丁语 ultra，以及现代英语由 outrage 衍生出的词。

normal.en: Outrage opens with out, and its Latin root ultra also means beyond: the act goes beyond all limits.
normal.cn: outrage 以 out 开头，其拉丁词根 ultra 同样表示「超出」：越界之举就是暴行。

normal.en: The rage inside is a trap: the word has nothing to do with anger being built from rage.
normal.cn: 词里的 rage 是个陷阱：outrage 并非由 rage（狂怒）构成，只是拼写相似。

normal.en: We say public outrage when a whole society reacts to an unfair act.
normal.cn: 当整个社会对不公之举做出反应时，我们说 public outrage。

normal.en: Outrageous and outraged both come from this word, one for the act and one for the feeling.
normal.cn: outrageous 与 outraged 都来自本词：一个形容行为离谱，一个形容人被激怒。

normal.en: In legal and political style, an outrage against the law means an attack on it.
normal.cn: 在法律与政治的文体里，an outrage against the law 意为对法律的践踏。

abstract.en: Picture a scale pushed far off balance by a heavy blow, and a crowd standing round it with tight fists.
abstract.cn: 想象天平被重物狠狠砸得失去平衡，围着它的人群攥紧了拳头。

abstract.en: Think of a line drawn on the ground: the outrage is the foot that steps far past it.
abstract.cn: 想象地上画着一条线：暴行就是一脚踩过线很远。

abstract.en: See the blow first, then the heat rising from the crowd: the same word names both the act and the anger.
abstract.cn: 先看到那一击，再看到人群里升起的热浪：同一个词既指行为，也指愤怒。

examples.en: The new tax caused public outrage.
examples.cn: 新税引发了公众的愤慨。

examples.en: Many people were outraged by the way the workers were treated.
examples.cn: 许多人对工人所受的待遇感到愤慨。

examples.en: The court called the destruction of the old library an outrage.
examples.cn: 法院把毁掉老图书馆的行为称为暴行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特雷基」——奥特战士雷厉风行、怒不可遏，众人也跟着愤慨；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 经古法语 outrage（过分、暴行）来自拉丁语 ultra（超出、在更远处）+ 法语后缀 -age；法语 u 在英语中读作 o。与英语 rage（狂怒）拼写相似但无词源关系。outrage 最初指越界之举，后来也指随之而起的愤慨，并转作动词。

sensesIntro.en: Outrage begins as an act that goes beyond every limit, then names unfair treatment, the anger such acts ignite, and finally the verb for causing that anger.
sensesIntro.cn: outrage 起初指越过一切界限的行为，随后用于不公的待遇，再指由此燃起的愤怒，最后转为引发愤怒的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale smashed far off balance while a crowd clenches its fists.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平被砸得严重失衡，围观的人攥紧了拳头。

branches.en: THE DEED: a cruel act goes past the limit of decency.
branches.cn: 行为层面：残忍之举越过了体面的界限。

branches.en: THE RULING: unfair rules and punished people count as outrages too.
branches.cn: 裁决层面：不公的规则与受罚的弱者同样算作 outrage。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the anger that rises in response is named with the same word.
branches.cn: 情绪层面：随之升起的愤怒也用同一个词来称呼。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the verb names the act of making others feel that anger.
branches.cn: 动作层面：动词表达的就是「使他人产生这种愤怒」。

branches.en: An outrage done and outrage felt are two sides of the same breach.
branches.cn: 越界之举与由此而生的愤慨，是同一次越界的两面。

intro.en: Outrage is borrowed from French, so its parts are French: a stem from ultra, beyond, and the noun suffix -age, later turning into a verb in English.
intro.cn: outrage 借自法语，构词成分都是法语的：来自 ultra（超出）的词干加名词后缀 -age，英语再把它转为动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultra, beyond, is recorded, and it also gives the modern prefix ultra-; the rest of the word is French word building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ultra（超出）有文献记录，也给出现代前缀 ultra-；其余部分属于法语的构词。

items.example: Ultra is the Latin source of the first part of outrage.
items.exampleCN: ultra 是 outrage 前半部分的拉丁来源。

items.example: The prefix ultra- survives in ultra-modern.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ultra- 保留在 ultra-modern 中。

items.example: The suffix -age turns the stem into an excess.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 把词干变成「过分之举」。

items.meaning: a cruel act or deep anger
items.example: Outrage carries both the act and the feeling.
items.exampleCN: outrage 同时承载行为与感受。

items.example: The suffix -d gives outraged.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -d 构成 outraged。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous gives outrageous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 outrageous。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives outrageously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 outrageously。

items.example: The suffix -ness gives outrageousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 outrageousness。

items.example: Rage looks related to outrage but is not its base.
items.exampleCN: rage 看似与本词相关，却并非它的词基。

definition_zh: 卖得比……多；销量超过；比……更能推销
definition_en: to sell more than another product, company, or person, or to do so by persuasion
core_image: 两个柜台并排放着同样的货，一边的队伍越排越长
scene: 两家书店卖同一本畅销书，西边那家一周卖掉的数量压过了东边那家。The new store outsells its rival on the same street.
sceneCN: 这里 outsell 是「卖得比……多」（第 1 个义项：销量超过同类）；句意：这条街上的新店卖得比对手多。

pos.zh: 比……更能推销；靠推销胜过

collocations.zh: 在每个市场上都卖得更好
超过所有其他品牌的销量

derivatives.zh: 由 sell 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「卖方；卖得好的商品」
由 sell 加 -ing 构成，义为「销售；推销」，即动名词形式
与 sell 同源于古英语 sellan，义为「销售；售出」

senses.title: To sell more than a rival
senses.definition: to sell a larger number or value of goods than another product, shop, or company
senses.definitionCN: 卖出比另一种产品、另一家商店或另一家公司更多数量或更高金额的商品
senses.example: Online editions now outsell printed copies of the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 现在这份报纸的网络版卖得比纸质版多。
senses.why: Out- here carries the idea of beyond, so the counting of sales runs past the rival figure.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 out- 带有「超出」的意思，于是销售的数量越过了对手的那个数字。

senses.title: To beat someone by selling
senses.definition: to defeat a person or team by making more sales in a contest or over a period
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛或某一时期内靠卖出更多商品而战胜某人或某个团队
senses.example: In the summer contest, she outsold every colleague in the branch.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季竞赛中，她卖出的货比支店里任何同事都多。
senses.why: The word hides winning inside selling, so the business act becomes a competition that one side wins.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「赢」藏在「卖」里面，于是商业行为变成了一场比赛，一方获胜。

senses.title: To win by persuasion
senses.titleCN: 凭说服力胜过；推销上赢过
senses.definition: to overcome someone through the force of argument or sales talk rather than by price
senses.definitionCN: 不是靠价格，而是靠论据或推销话术的力量说服并胜过某人
senses.example: The agent managed to outsell her on the phone that afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 那天下午，那位代理人靠电话成功地说服了她、卖得比她好。
senses.why: Selling also means persuading, so out- can mean outwitting someone in talk.
senses.whyCN: sell 也有「说服」之义，所以 out- 可以表示在言谈上胜过对方。

senses.title: To have larger sales than usual
senses.definition: to record a higher number of sales than an earlier period, often used with soft sell or record terms
senses.definitionCN: 录得比先前某段时期更高的销售数字，常用于「软性推销」或「创纪录」等说法
senses.example: Hardback editions usually outsell themselves in the week before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 精装版本通常在假期前一周销量好于往年同期。
senses.why: Without an explicit competitor, out- points back to the earlier record rather than to another firm.
senses.whyCN: 没有明说对手时，out- 指回的是先前的记录，而不是另一家公司。

senses.title: To be more sought after
senses.definition: to be in greater demand than something else, so that buyers turn to it first
senses.definitionCN: 比别的东西更被需要，买主会优先选择它
senses.example: The smaller car outsells the big one at this price.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个价位上，那辆小车比大车更抢手。
senses.why: More sales is the visible trace of stronger demand, so the verb shades into meaning in demand.
senses.whyCN: 更高的销量是需求更旺的可见痕迹，所以这个词渐渐有了「更受欢迎」之意。

senses.title: To sell out of stock first
senses.definition: to reach a sold out state before a competing product does
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争产品之前进入售罄状态
senses.example: Its tickets outsold the next concert and vanished in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 它的票比下一场音乐会的票先卖完，一小时内就没了。
senses.why: When two counters both run out, the faster one wins, so out- becomes the one that empties first.
senses.whyCN: 两个柜台都卖到缺货时，快的一方就赢了，于是 out- 表示先卖空。

senses.title: To exceed one by a stated amount
senses.definition: to exceed another by a stated figure or percentage, often followed by by
senses.definitionCN: 以某个数字或百分比超出对方，后面常接 by
senses.example: The local brand outsells imports by nearly three to one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个本地品牌的销量是进口商品的三倍左右。
senses.why: The basic verb is comparative, so a by phrase naturally supplies the size of the lead.
senses.whyCN: 它本身就是比较性的动词，所以 by 短语自然用来补出领先的幅度。

intro.en: Outsell is an English invention that joins out- with sell, and the participle outsold is far older than the verb itself.
intro.cn: outsell 是英语自身造出的词，由 out- 与 sell 组合而成，其中过去分词 outsold 的用法远早于动词本身。

items.en: Sellan means to give something to another for money.
items.cn: 古英语 sellan 意为把东西换取钱财交给别人，即「卖」。

items.en: Out- already means beyond or surpassing, as in outlive and outnumber.
items.cn: 16 世纪时 out- 已意为「超过、胜过」，如 outlive、outnumber。

items.en: The participle outsold appears earlier, describing goods that went for more money.
items.cn: 过去分词 outsold 先出现，用来描述卖得价更高或卖得更多的货物。

items.en: Outsell becomes a regular verb of commerce, meaning to sell more than another.
items.cn: 19 世纪 outsell 成为常规的商业动词，意为卖得比……多。

items.en: The word spreads to advertising, sport, and publishing talk of beating rivals.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到广告、体育和出版业，用来表示胜过对手。

items.en: Today it is the standard comparative form of the verb sell.
items.cn: 今天它是动词 sell 的标准比较式。

note.en: Outsell is one of a large out- family, and it sits near words for sales, winning, and persuading.
note.cn: outsell 属于庞大的 out- 词族，它的邻居包括与销售、取胜、说服有关的词。

entries.definition: to spend more money than another
to be greater in number than another
to praise something too highly, or to sell more than can be supplied

normalIntro.en: Outsell reads as out plus sell: the sales figure steps out in front of the other one.
normalIntro.cn: outsell 可以拆成 out 加 sell：销售数字站到了对手的前面。

normal.en: Out- is the productive prefix meaning beyond or better than, as in outnumber and outlive.
normal.cn: out- 是能产的表示「超过、胜过」的前缀，见于 outnumber 与 outlive。

normal.en: Its past tense outsold is irregular, so it changes sell into sold inside the word.
normal.cn: 它的过去式 outsold 是不规则的，于是词里的 sell 变成了 sold。

normal.en: The verb is almost always transitive, so it needs an object such as rivals or imports.
normal.cn: 这个动词几乎总是及物，所以需要 rivals 或 imports 这类宾语。

normal.en: The by phrase measures the lead, as in outsells imports by three to one.
normal.cn: by 短语用来量出领先的幅度，如「销量是进口货的三倍」。

normal.en: Compare oversell, where over- means too much rather than more than another.
normal.cn: 对比 oversell：那里的 over- 表示「过分」，而不是「超过别人」。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf graph where one bar climbs past the other and keeps rising.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上的销量柱状图，一根柱子越过另一根还在往上蹿。

abstract.en: Imagine two shopkeepers counting coins side by side at closing time.
abstract.cn: 想象两个店主在打烊时并排数钱，一边的硬币堆更高。

abstract.en: Think of a phone call in which one voice wins the customer by talking.
abstract.cn: 想象一通电话里，一个声音靠说话把顾客争取了过来。

examples.en: The toy outsold every other game that Christmas.
examples.cn: 那个圣诞节这款玩具比其他任何游戏都卖得好。

examples.en: Small cars have outsold large ones for years in this market.
examples.cn: 多年来在这个市场里小车的销量一直超过大车。

examples.en: Reviews suggest the film will outsell its two competitors easily.
examples.cn: 评论界的看法是，这部电影会轻松卖得比两个竞争对手多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬特 sell」——商家熬夜特卖，所以卖得比别家多；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: out-（出、超过）+ sell（古英语 sellan，卖）：卖到超出对方，即「比……卖得多」；同族有 outsold、outspend、outnumber。

sensesIntro.en: Outsell starts with the plain comparison of sales, then adds beating a person, winning by persuasion, beating a record, being in demand, selling out first, and the by amount.
sensesIntro.cn: outsell 先从最直接的销量比较出发，再扩展到胜过某人、靠说服取胜、超过以往记录、更受追捧、先卖完，以及用 by 表示超出多少。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two counters side by side, and one queue keeps growing.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个柜台并排摆着，一边的队伍越排越长。

branches.en: The plain comparative sense counts goods sold against another figure.
branches.cn: 最基础的比较义，是把卖出的货与另一个数字对照。

branches.en: Beating a person turns the comparison into a contest with a winner.
branches.cn: 胜过一个人，把比较变成了一场有赢家的比赛。

branches.en: Selling as persuading lets the verb mean winning the argument on the phone.
branches.cn: sell 有「说服」之义，于是这个词可以指在电话里赢下争论。

branches.en: Without a rival, out- points to an earlier record or to emptying stock first.
branches.cn: 没有对手时，out- 指向先前的记录，或者指向先卖空库存。

branches.en: The comparative core also yields in demand and a stated margin of lead.
branches.cn: 比较的核心还衍生出「抢手」以及用数字标出的领先幅度。

intro.en: Outsell is built from the prefix out- and the verb sell, both native English elements.
intro.cn: outsell 由前缀 out- 与动词 sell 两部分构成，两者都是英语本族元素。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Germanic, so Latin contributes only through later literary borrowing such as exceed.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个部分属于日耳曼语源，拉丁语只是通过后来借入的 exceed 等文学词汇间接相关。

definition_zh: 伸开；伸展；伸向；超出（限度）
definition_en: to stretch something out or spread a thing out at full length; also to extend past a limit
core_image: 双臂向两侧完全展开，手指伸到再也不能伸得更远
scene: 起点线前的短跑选手把双臂向两侧伸开，等着发令枪响。The sprinter outstretched both arms behind the starting line.
sceneCN: 这里 outstretch 是「伸开」（第 1 个义项：把东西或肢体整个伸展铺开）；句意：那名短跑选手把双臂在起跑线后方伸展开。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，古英语 streccan 意为「伸展」，可作动词或名词
由 stretch 加 -er 构成，指把人伸直抬运的「担架」
由 stretch 加 -y 构成，义为「有弹性的；能拉长的」

senses.title: To stretch out to full length
senses.definition: to extend an arm, a limb, or a piece of cloth so that it is held out at its full length
senses.definitionCN: 把手臂、肢体或一块布向外伸展，直到完全拉长展开
senses.example: He outstretched his arms to catch the falling child.
senses.exampleCN: 他伸开双臂去接住跌落的孩子。
senses.why: Out- supplies the outward push and stretch supplies the pulling apart, so together they mean press out to the limit.
senses.whyCN: out- 提供向外推出的力量，stretch 提供拉开的动作，合起来就是把东西推到极限地展开。

senses.title: To lie extended so as to cover ground
senses.definition: to lie stretched across a surface or a distance, as a plain or a road does
senses.definitionCN: 像平原或道路那样，铺展在某个表面或距离之上
senses.example: A plain outstretched before the travellers, with no trees in sight.
senses.exampleCN: 一片平原在他们面前展开，一眼望去看不到树。
senses.why: The participle adds the positional sense, describing landscape that lies open and wide.
senses.whyCN: 分词形式又带出位置感，用来描写平铺开阔的地貌。

senses.title: To reach toward something
senses.definition: to push a hand or object forward and outward toward a person or goal
senses.definitionCN: 把手或物朝某人或某个目标向前向外伸过去
senses.example: She outstretched her hand toward the doorknob.
senses.exampleCN: 她朝门把手伸出手去。
senses.why: Stretching always implies distance, so the out- part naturally points the motion at a target.
senses.whyCN: 伸展本身就含距离，所以 out- 这一半自然把动作指向一个目标。

senses.title: To become longer or wider than expected
senses.titleCN: 拉得过长；变得比预期更宽
senses.definition: to become longer or wider than intended because it is stretched too far
senses.definitionCN: 因为拉伸过度而变得比原意更长或更宽
senses.example: The old sweater had outstretched at the cuffs.
senses.exampleCN: 那件旧毛衣的袖口被拉大了。
senses.why: When stretch goes past its proper point, out- reads as beyond the intended measure.
senses.whyCN: 当拉伸超过了合适的程度，out- 就读成「超出了原本的尺度」。

senses.title: To make a straight line taut
senses.definition: to pull a rope or wire tight so that it forms a straight line
senses.definitionCN: 把绳或金属线拉紧，使之成为一条直线
senses.example: They outstretched a wire between the two posts.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在两根柱子之间拉直了一条铁丝。
senses.why: The stretching is now controlled, producing the clean line that out- suggests.
senses.whyCN: 此时的拉伸是有控制的，于是出现了 out- 所暗示的那条挺直的线。

senses.title: To extend beyond a limit
senses.definition: to go past the normal limits of something such as patience or a load
senses.definitionCN: 走过某物如耐心或负载的通常限度
senses.example: Their long delays outstretched the patience of the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一再拖延，超出了全班人的耐心。
senses.why: The freedom that made out- mean forward also lets it mean past the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 让 out- 表示「向前」的那种自由，也让它能表示「越过边界」。

senses.title: To throw or cast forward
senses.definition: to cast an arm or an object forward and outward, as in a throw or a gesture
senses.definitionCN: 像投掷或做手势那样，把手或物向前向外送出去
senses.example: He outstretched his arm to launch the dart.
senses.exampleCN: 他伸出手臂把飞镖投了出去。
senses.why: A throw is a sudden outward stretch, so the verb lends itself to gestures of casting.
senses.whyCN: 投掷就是一次突然的向外伸展，所以这个词也用于各类抛掷和手势。

intro.en: Outstretch is a plain English compound of out- and stretch, both of native origin, with no Latin ancestry.
intro.cn: outstretch 是 out- 与 stretch 组成的英语复合词，两部分都源于本族语，与拉丁语无直接亲缘关系。

items.en: Streccan means to stretch, spread, or extend a limb or a surface.
items.cn: 古英语 streccan 意为伸、展、铺开肢体或表面。

items.en: Out already means away or outward, used with many verbs.
items.cn: 古英语的 out 已表示向外、出去，常与动词连用。

items.en: Outstretched arises first as a participle describing limbs and hands.
items.cn: 14 世纪时 outstretched 先以分词形式出现，用于描写手臂和手。

items.en: The verb outstretch follows, used of arms, branches, and ropes.
items.cn: 随后出现动词 outstretch，用于手臂、树枝和绳子。

items.en: The form appears in poetry and prose to describe open landscapes and long shadows.
items.cn: 19 世纪这一形式见于诗歌与散文，用来写开阔的风景和长长的影子。

items.en: Today it is mainly literary, though the participle outstretched is common in prose.
items.cn: 如今它偏文学化，但分词 outstretched 在散文中仍很常用。

note.en: Outstretch belongs to the stretch family and sits beside verbs of reaching, spreading, and remaining unreached.
note.cn: outstretch 属于 stretch 词族，它的邻居包括伸展、铺开以及「未被超越」这类词。

entries.definition: the act of helping or contacting people in the community
entries.definitionCN: 对外开展的服务与联络（与 outstretch 词源不同，只是拼写相近）
